difficulty:0.en: Inside the map room, Old Helm spread the newest fragment across the table. Every edge matched a star-line we had traced the night before. But reading the old ink was a *difficulty* none of us had expected — the symbols shifted like smoke whenever the lantern flickered.
difficulty:0.cnHint: 老舵手在地图室里研究新碎片，发现辨认古老符文有很大的____。
difficulty:0.hook: The last symbol pulsed once, then went completely dark.
difficulty:0.line: 'The *difficulty* is not the ink — it is the light we read it by,' said Old Helm.

full:0.en: The lantern shelf above the chart table was *full* of tiny glass bottles, each holding a captured starlight-drop. Old Helm said every bottle was a promise made on a different island. I counted thirty-seven promises and wondered how many were still kept.
full:0.cnHint: 地图室的架子上____是装着星光的小瓶子，每一个都藏着一段旧约定。
full:0.hook: Bottle thirty-eight was empty, yet still faintly warm.
full:0.line: 'A shelf *full* of promises is heavier than it looks,' Old Helm said softly.

range:0.en: Bell had drawn a circle on the chart showing the *range* of the falling stars we had watched that evening. Within that circle sat four islands we had never visited. She tapped the nearest one and smiled, as if she already knew its name and was simply waiting for us to catch up.
range:0.cnHint: 领航员在图上标出流星的____，发现圆圈内有四座从未踏访的岛屿。
range:0.hook: One of those islands was not on any earlier map.
range:0.line: 'That *range* covers more islands than our whole journey so far,' Bell said.

region:0.en: Old Helm pointed to a shadowed corner of the chart and said the falling stars came from that *region* of the sky every hundred years. The air in the map room felt thicker just looking at it. Bell quietly moved her finger away, then moved it back, as if she could not help herself.
region:0.cnHint: 老舵手指出，流星来自星图上某个特定的____，每百年才出现一次。
region:0.hook: Something in that region was already moving toward us.
region:0.line: 'No troupe has ever charted that *region* and returned the same,' said Old Helm.

material:0.en: In the corner of the map room stood a chest of *material* salvaged from wrecked sky-ships — scraps of sail, bent compass needles, and a piece of hull wood that glowed faint blue at night. Old Helm said the glow meant the wood still remembered its home island and had not given up looking.
material:0.cnHint: 地图室角落的箱子里存放着从残骸中salvaged的各种____，其中一块木头在夜里发出微光。
material:0.hook: The blue glow brightened the moment we named our next destination.
material:0.line: 'Good *material* keeps the memory of where it came from,' said Old Helm.

pressure:0.en: Bell was fixing the altitude gauge on the wall when she warned us not to touch the brass valve beside it. The *pressure* inside was high enough to crack the casing if the seal was loose. We all stepped back at once, then laughed a little at how quickly we had moved.
pressure:0.cnHint: 领航员修理高度仪时提醒大家别碰阀门，因为里面的____大到危险。
pressure:0.hook: Then the needle crept past the red line on its own.
pressure:0.line: 'The *pressure* has been climbing since the stars started falling,' Bell said.

thus:0.en: The map fragment glowed when Old Helm placed it next to the altitude gauge, and the gauge needle swung to the east. He had never seen the two react to each other before. *Thus* the falling stars were not just a show — they were a signal pointing us toward the next island.
thus:0.cnHint: 地图碎片与高度仪产生了奇妙的反应，____大家意识到流星其实是一种指引。
thus:0.hook: East held an island none of us had dared name aloud.
thus:0.line: 'The stars fall, the needle swings — *thus* we have our heading,' said Old Helm.

tool:0.en: Bell kept every navigator's *tool* in a flat wooden case lined with dark cloth — compass, measure-string, star-wheel, and a small lens ground from island crystal. She cleaned each one slowly while the rest of us talked, and I noticed she listened most carefully when her hands were busiest.
tool:0.cnHint: 领航员将每件导航____整齐地收在木盒里，一边擦拭一边专注地聆听大家的讨论。
tool:0.hook: She stopped cleaning and looked up at exactly the right moment.
tool:0.line: 'A *tool* only earns its place the day you truly need it,' Bell said.

international:0.en: Inside the map room, Old Helm unrolled a chart covered in stamps from dozens of islands. 'This,' he said proudly, 'is an *international* record — every trading port between the eastern winds and the western clouds.' I traced the tiny ink marks with one finger, feeling the weight of so many journeys.
international:0.cnHint: 老船长在地图室里展示一张盖满各地印章的航海图，说明它具有____性的意义。
international:0.hook: One stamp, darker than the rest, had no name beneath it.
international:0.line: 'This is an *international* chart — every port between the winds.'

manage:0.en: The lantern above the supply shelf flickered and went dark. Bell stood on a crate, reached into the shadows, and twisted the oil cap with steady hands. 'I can *manage* it,' she said quietly. A moment later warm light filled the room again, and she stepped down with a small satisfied smile.
manage:0.cnHint: 小铃在储藏室里独自____修好了熄灭的灯，没有请任何人帮忙。
manage:0.hook: But behind the shelf, something had been quietly listening.
manage:0.line: 'Don't worry — I can *manage* it on my own.'

outside:0.en: Rain tapped the wooden walls of our resting cabin. Old Helm spread tomorrow's route across the table while Bell sketched wind notes in her log. The *outside* was cold and wet, but in here the candles were bright and the tea was hot, and the whole troupe felt strangely, perfectly safe.
outside:0.cnHint: 夜雨敲打着小木屋，大家在温暖的室内规划明日的航线，____寒冷而潮湿。
outside:0.hook: Then the rain stopped — all at once, completely without warning.
outside:0.line: 'The *outside* is cold, so stay close to the candles tonight.'

fun:0.en: Old Helm pulled out a worn deck of word cards and dealt them around the table. 'A little *fun* before sleep,' he announced, grinning. Each card showed a place none of us had visited. We laughed, argued over pronunciations, and forgot for a while that we were drifting miles above the ground.
fun:0.cnHint: 出发前夕，老船长拿出一副单词卡牌，让大家在室内享受____、放松心情。
fun:0.hook: The last card in the deck showed an island none of us recognised.
fun:0.line: 'A little *fun* never hurt anyone — deal the cards!'

reality:0.en: I had imagined the chart room as something grand — tall shelves, golden instruments, a ceiling full of maps. The *reality* was a low, cosy space with ink-stained walls and mismatched chairs. Old Helm watched my face and laughed softly. 'The best rooms,' he said, 'are always smaller than the dream.'
reality:0.cnHint: 我幻想中的海图室富丽堂皇，但____却是一间低矮朴素的小屋。
reality:0.hook: Yet one corner held a door I had not noticed before.
reality:0.line: 'The *reality* is small — but every great journey started here.'

beyond:0.en: Bell pointed to the far edge of the planning chart, where the ink faded into blank space. 'What lies *beyond* that border?' I asked. She shook her head slowly. 'Nothing written yet,' she said, tapping the empty paper. 'That is exactly why we keep moving.' Old Helm refilled our cups in quiet agreement.
beyond:0.cnHint: 小铃指着地图边缘的空白区域，说明那片____边界的地方还无人记录。
beyond:0.hook: The blank space seemed, just for a moment, to shimmer.
beyond:0.line: 'What lies *beyond* that border is ours to discover.'

completely:0.en: I tried to copy Bell's knot — the one that held the navigation lantern in place. After four failed attempts I was *completely* lost, fingers tangled in rope. Bell sat beside me without a word and guided my hands step by step until the knot held firm. It was a small thing, but it felt like progress.
completely:0.cnHint: 我学小铃打绳结时____不得要领，最后在她的手把手指导下才成功。
completely:0.hook: Bell glanced at the lantern and said nothing more, only smiled.
completely:0.line: 'I was *completely* lost until you showed me that second loop.'

advise:0.en: Before we left the supply room, Old Helm paused at the door. 'I *advise* you to sleep early tonight,' he said, looking at me with calm, serious eyes. 'Tomorrow the stars will shift, and anyone still tired will miss the moment they change.' I nodded and climbed to my bunk without argument.
advise:0.cnHint: 老船长在离开储藏室前____我早点休息，因为明晚星辰将发生变化。
advise:0.hook: I lay awake wondering what exactly the stars would change into.
advise:0.line: 'I *advise* you to sleep early — the stars shift at dawn.'

consume:0.en: Inside the troupe's warm cabin, the old wood stove crackled through the night. Old Helm warned us that a single storm could *consume* all our lamp oil before dawn. We checked every bottle twice, counting drops as if they were gold coins.
consume:0.cnHint: 老赫姆警告说，一场风暴可能会____掉所有的灯油。
consume:0.hook: One bottle was already half empty — and no one had touched it.
consume:0.line: 'A single bad night can *consume* everything we have saved,' Old Helm said quietly.

desire:0.en: Bell spread the star chart across the table and traced a faint line toward the eastern islands. Her eyes held a quiet fire. 'I *desire* to reach that cluster before the season turns,' she said. Old Helm nodded, folding his hands around his warm cup.
desire:0.cnHint: 贝尔____着在季节变换前抵达那片群岛。
desire:0.hook: But the chart showed a gap where no island had ever been named.
desire:0.line: 'I *desire* to see what waits beyond that last star,' Bell whispered.

meal:0.en: After a long day of mending sails, the troupe gathered around the low table. The *meal* was simple — warm broth, flat bread, and dried fruit — but every face softened as steam rose in the lamplight. Even Silverfang, who rarely smiled, reached for a second bowl.
meal:0.cnHint: 经过漫长的一天，船员们围坐在一起享用这顿____。
meal:0.hook: Then a sharp knock echoed from the cabin door — no one was expected tonight.
meal:0.line: 'A good *meal* after hard work is the best reward,' Old Helm said warmly.

vegetable:0.en: I found a small clay pot on the window ledge, holding a single bright *vegetable* — a green shoot Old Helm called a 'sky-leek.' He said it only grew on the highest islands and that its smell could calm a nervous crew on stormy nights.
vegetable:0.cnHint: 老赫姆在窗台上种着一株特殊的____，据说能让船员在风雨夜镇定下来。
vegetable:0.hook: The shoot had doubled in size overnight, and no one had watered it.
vegetable:0.line: 'That *vegetable* has sailed with me for ten years,' Old Helm said with a smile.

adopt:0.en: Old Helm called us together and said the troupe needed a new rule: we would *adopt* a habit of writing one word on the map before sleeping each night. 'Words are our compass,' he said. Bell handed me the pen first, and the whole cabin felt warmer.
adopt:0.cnHint: 老赫姆提议大家____一个新习惯，每晚睡前在地图上写下一个词语。
adopt:0.hook: The word I wrote seemed to glow faintly against the old parchment.
adopt:0.line: 'We will *adopt* this rule tonight and keep it every night,' Old Helm declared.

miss:0.en: Bell set the lantern on the table and showed me the map fragment we had found. 'A new *miss* in navigation, even a small one, and we drift past the island entirely,' she said, pointing to a thin blue line. I promised to watch the stars more carefully.
miss:0.cnHint: 贝尔解释说，一次导航上的____就会让我们与目标岛屿擦肩而过。
miss:0.hook: She then pointed to a mark on the map that had not been there yesterday.
miss:0.line: 'One *miss* at the helm and the stars will not forgive us,' Bell said calmly.

yourself:0.en: Old Helm handed me the log book without a word. I looked up, unsure. He tapped the blank page and said, 'Write it *yourself* — what you saw, what you felt, what surprised you today.' It was the first time the record was truly mine, and my hand shook a little.
yourself:0.cnHint: 老赫姆让我亲自用____记录下今天所见所感。
yourself:0.hook: When I opened the book, someone had already written my name on the first line.
yourself:0.line: 'You must learn to trust *yourself* before you trust the map,' Old Helm said.

century:0.en: On the oldest shelf in the cabin sat a glass jar sealed with red wax. Old Helm said the jar had travelled with the troupe for nearly a *century*, passed from one leader to the next. Inside, pressed flat, was the very first word fragment the troupe had ever collected.
century:0.cnHint: 船舱里有一个密封玻璃罐，据说已随剧团旅行了近一个____。
century:0.hook: Tonight, for the first time, a thin crack had appeared along the wax seal.
century:0.line: 'This jar has kept our first word safe for almost a *century*,' Old Helm said softly.

responsibility:0.en: The map room inside the old lighthouse smelled of candle wax and old paper. Old Helm spread the latest chart across the table and looked at me with steady eyes. 'Every word we collect carries weight,' he said. 'That *responsibility* belongs to all of us now.' I felt the words settle into my chest like stones finding the bottom of a still lake.
responsibility:0.cnHint: 老舵手告诉我，收集每一个词语都是整个团队需要承担的____。
responsibility:0.hook: Outside, a single star broke loose and fell toward the eastern island.
responsibility:0.line: 'That *responsibility* belongs to all of us now.'

soon:0.en: Bell leaned over her navigation table, candles burning low on both sides. She traced a thin line across the floating chart with one finger. 'We will reach the Amber Shelf,' she said quietly, 'but not tonight.' I watched the flame flicker and felt the waiting press softly against my ribs. *Soon* was a word that held both promise and patience.
soon:0.cnHint: 领航员说，我们____就能抵达琥珀岛架，但今晚还不行。
soon:0.hook: Then the candles bent sideways, as if the air itself had leaned in to listen.
soon:0.line: 'We will get there *soon* — trust the map and trust the wind.'

center:0.en: Old Helm unrolled a star chart so wide it covered the whole floor. At its *center* was a blank circle — no island drawn, no name written, only empty space ringed by careful notes. 'That blank spot,' Bell said from the doorway, 'is where everything we have collected is pointing.' I stood at the edge of the chart and felt the pull.
center:0.cnHint: 星图的____是一片空白，那正是所有线索指向的神秘之处。
center:0.hook: The blank circle began, very slowly, to glow.
center:0.line: 'Everything on the chart points toward this *center*.'

arrive:0.en: We had been travelling for three days when the anchor finally dropped. I pressed my face to the porthole and saw soft golden light spilling from a domed building on the island below. 'We *arrive* at last,' Old Helm said, setting down his cup. The troupe moved quickly, gathering word-fragments and map pieces, ready to step onto new ground.
arrive:0.cnHint: 经过三天的旅程，我们终于____了那座发出金色光芒的圆顶建筑所在的岛屿。
arrive:0.hook: But the door of the domed building was already open, and footprints led inside.
arrive:0.line: 'We *arrive* at last — keep your word-fragments close.'

boost:0.en: Bell handed me a small glowing stone she had taken from the word-vault shelf. 'Hold it while you read the fragment,' she said. 'It gives your memory a *boost*.' The moment the stone touched my palm, the old letters on the page seemed sharper, brighter, as if someone had turned up the light behind each word. I read the whole fragment without stopping.
boost:0.cnHint: 领航员给了我一块发光的石头，它能给记忆一个____，让我更清晰地阅读古老的词语碎片。
boost:0.hook: When I finished reading, the stone turned cold and the shelf behind me creaked open.
boost:0.line: 'That little stone gives your memory a real *boost*.'

conflict:0.en: Silverfang arrived at the door of the map room just as Old Helm was sealing a newly found word inside its case. The two stood facing each other, and the air between them felt tight. Their ideas about which route to take did not match, and every quiet word seemed to *conflict* with the last. I held the word-case and waited, hoping the silence would break gently.
conflict:0.cnHint: 老舵手和竞争船长的路线选择____了，整个地图室的气氛变得紧张起来。
conflict:0.hook: Then Bell stepped between them, holding a single candle, and neither man spoke.
conflict:0.line: 'Our plans *conflict* — but the sky will settle this for us.'

demand:0.en: Silverfang crossed his arms and looked at the shelf of locked word-cases along the wall. 'I will trade you fair passage,' he said, 'but I *demand* the fragment from the northern vault in return.' Old Helm did not answer at once. He poured two cups of tea instead, placed one in front of Silverfang, and let the silence do its own talking.
demand:0.cnHint: 竞争船长____得到北方金库中的词语碎片，作为提供安全通道的条件。
demand:0.hook: Old Helm's hand rested on the vault key, but he had not yet moved it.
demand:0.line: 'I *demand* the northern fragment — that is my only price.'

emotion:0.en: After the long argument faded and Silverfang had gone, Old Helm sat alone at the table, turning an empty cup in his hands. I had never seen his face carry so much *emotion* — not anger, not sadness exactly, but something layered, like weather changing over open water. Bell put a hand briefly on his shoulder, then went back to her charts without a word.
emotion:0.cnHint: 争论结束后，老舵手独自坐在桌边，脸上流露出复杂的____，令我从未见过。
emotion:0.hook: On the chart in front of him, a new word had appeared all on its own.
emotion:0.line: 'Do not hide your *emotion* — the crew needs to know you are human too.'

management:0.en: Inside the map room, Old Helm spread charts across a wide table. Every island, every route — all recorded. 'Good *management* of our charts means we never lose our way,' he said. Bell nodded, tracing a finger along the edge of the newest fragment, already thinking ahead to the next island.
management:0.cnHint: 老舵在地图室里向我展示舰队的____方式，小铃若有所思地看着最新的地图碎片。
management:0.hook: But one chart showed an island none of us had marked.
management:0.line: 'Good *management* of our charts means we never lose our way.'

perfect:0.en: Bell held the new word-fragment up to the lantern light. The edges matched the old chart so cleanly it was almost unbelievable. 'This is *perfect*,' she whispered. Old Helm leaned in, eyes bright. Even the ink colour matched. Together, the two pieces revealed a path none of us had dared hope existed.
perfect:0.cnHint: 小铃发现新的词语碎片与旧地图____契合，拼出了一条从未预料到的路线。
perfect:0.hook: The path led straight into the heart of the falling stars.
perfect:0.line: 'This fit is *perfect* — as if the two pieces were always meant to meet.'

along:0.en: We gathered *along* the curved wall of the ship's lower cabin, each of us holding a lantern. Old Helm unrolled the latest chart on the floor. The islands formed a chain, one after another, like notes in a quiet song. Bell pointed to the gap in the middle and said nothing.
along:0.cnHint: 我们____弧形船舱内壁站成一排，老舵展开地图，小铃指着中间那片空白沉默不语。
along:0.hook: In the gap, a faint shape flickered — then vanished.
along:0.line: 'Stand *along* this wall so everyone can see the chart clearly.'

harm:0.en: Old Helm warned us to keep the word-fragments away from the engine's heat. 'Damp or flame could *harm* them beyond repair,' he said quietly, wrapping each piece in soft cloth. Bell stacked them into the wooden case with steady hands. I watched, realising for the first time how fragile our whole map really was.
harm:0.cnHint: 老舵叮嘱大家妥善保管词语碎片，因为高温或潮湿都会____它们。
harm:0.hook: Then we heard a hiss — something near the engine had shifted.
harm:0.line: 'Heat and water can *harm* these fragments beyond any repair.'

increasingly:0.en: As night deepened, the cabin grew *increasingly* quiet. One by one, lanterns dimmed. Old Helm sat alone at the table, still studying the charts. I brought him a cup of warm water. He looked up, smiled briefly, and returned to his maps. Outside, stars were falling in long, slow lines across the dark sky.
increasingly:0.cnHint: 夜越来越深，船舱____安静，老舵独自坐在桌前研究地图，窗外星光划过长空。
increasingly:0.hook: One falling star traced the exact shape of our next route.
increasingly:0.line: 'The silence grows *increasingly* deep — even the stars seem to be listening.'

opinion:0.en: Bell placed two possible routes on the table and looked at each of us in turn. 'What is your *opinion*?' she asked. Old Helm tapped the northern path. I pointed to the southern one, where the star-glow was warmer. Bell smiled and folded both charts carefully. She had already made her choice — she just wanted us to feel heard.
opinion:0.cnHint: 小铃把两条路线摆在桌上，询问大家的____，但她心中早已有了答案。
opinion:0.hook: Her eyes lingered a second too long on a third route she had not shown us.
opinion:0.line: 'I want your *opinion* before I mark our course on the chart.'

previous:0.en: Old Helm pulled out a worn notebook filled with notes from *previous* voyages. Each page held a word-fragment sketch and a short description of the island it had unlocked. 'Every journey teaches something,' he said softly. Bell read over his shoulder, quiet and attentive. I copied a few lines into my own small book, just in case.
previous:0.cnHint: 老舵翻出记录____航行的旧笔记，里面画满了词语碎片和它们解锁的岛屿。
previous:0.hook: On the last page, a sketch matched the fragment we had just found tonight.
previous:0.line: 'Our *previous* voyages are all written here — nothing is truly forgotten.'

aim:0.en: Bell drew a small circle on the blank part of the chart. 'Our *aim* is to reach this point before the star-fall ends,' she said. Old Helm nodded slowly. The window glowed with falling light. I felt something settle inside me — a clear direction after days of drifting. We had a destination. That changed everything.
aim:0.cnHint: 小铃在地图上画了一个圆圈，说明我们此行的____是在星落结束前抵达那个地点。
aim:0.hook: The star-fall was already fading — we had less time than we thought.
aim:0.line: 'Our *aim* is clear: reach that island before the last star falls.'

model:0.en: Inside the map room, Old Helm placed a tiny *model* of the islands on the table. Every peak and bridge was perfectly shaped from wood and wire. 'Study this,' he said, 'and you will know where the next word hides.' I leaned closer, hardly breathing.
model:0.cnHint: 老舵手把一个浮岛的____摆在桌上，说它能指引下一个词的位置。
model:0.hook: One island on the model was already glowing faintly.
model:0.line: 'This *model* shows every island we have yet to visit.'

spot:0.en: Bell spread the star chart across the floor and began to *spot* tiny ink marks hidden among the constellations. Each mark was a word waiting to be claimed. 'There — and there,' she whispered, circling two distant islands with a trembling finger.
spot:0.cnHint: 领航员在星图上____隐藏的墨迹，那些都是还未被收集的词。
spot:0.hook: The third mark moved before she could circle it.
spot:0.line: 'I can *spot* two new words right here on the chart.'

achievement:0.en: Old Helm pinned a small token to the wall — one for every word the troupe had ever found. He called it the wall of *achievement*. Seeing so many tokens made my chest feel warm and wide. I had only added one, but it gleamed beside the rest.
achievement:0.cnHint: 老舵手把每次收集到词所获得的纪念章钉在墙上，称之为____之墙。
achievement:0.hook: There was one empty hook that no token had ever filled.
achievement:0.line: 'Every token here is a real *achievement* for our troupe.'

enter:0.en: To reach the inner library, we had to *enter* a narrow door carved with letters no one could read. Bell said the door only opened when you spoke a collected word aloud. I chose the first word I had ever found, and the hinges turned without a sound.
enter:0.cnHint: 要____内部书库，必须大声说出一个已收集的词，门才肯打开。
enter:0.hook: Beyond the door, the air smelled of somewhere very far away.
enter:0.line: 'Only those who carry a word may *enter* this room.'

eye:0.en: Old Helm had a sharp *eye* for detail that never seemed to rest. While the rest of us looked at the map, he studied the shadows the lantern cast on the ceiling. 'The shape up there,' he said quietly, 'matches the outline of an island we have not named yet.'
eye:0.cnHint: 老舵手用敏锐的____发现灯光投影在天花板上的图案竟是一座未命名的岛屿。
eye:0.hook: The shadow shifted, as if the island itself had moved.
eye:0.line: 'Keep a careful *eye* on the ceiling — something is forming.'

shift:0.en: Halfway through the night, Bell noticed a *shift* in the star pattern outside the porthole. The stars we used as guides had drifted a full hand-width to the left. 'The islands are moving,' she said, and immediately began redrawing the chart from the beginning.
shift:0.cnHint: 领航员察觉到舷窗外星星的位置发生了____，意识到浮岛正在漂移。
shift:0.hook: If the islands had moved, our marked path was already wrong.
shift:0.line: 'This *shift* in the stars means our map needs changing now.'

agree:0.en: Old Helm wanted to wait until dawn before opening the sealed chest. Silverfang said we should open it at once. I looked at Bell, and she gave a small nod. 'I *agree* with Silverfang,' I said, surprising myself. The room went quiet, and then Old Helm smiled slowly.
agree:0.cnHint: 老舵手和竞争船长对何时打开密封箱意见不一，叙述者选择了____其中一方。
agree:0.hook: Old Helm's slow smile meant he had expected that answer all along.
agree:0.line: 'I *agree* — waiting until dawn is too great a risk.'

aware:0.en: I was only half listening when Bell began to read the old log aloud. Then she paused. Suddenly I became *aware* that every name in the log matched the tokens on the achievement wall — every single one. The room felt smaller, as if the walls had leaned in to listen.
aware:0.cnHint: 叙述者在听领航员读旧航行日志时，突然____到日志里的名字与荣誉墙上完全吻合。
aware:0.hook: The last name in the log was one none of us had spoken yet.
aware:0.line: 'Are you *aware* that these names match every token on the wall?'

describe:0.en: Inside the map-room, Old Helm spread the latest fragment across the table. 'Try to *describe* what you see,' he said softly. The lines on the parchment shifted like rivers finding new beds. I leaned close, searching for words that could hold the shape of a place no one had named yet.
describe:0.cnHint: 老舵让我____地图碎片上奇异的图案。
describe:0.hook: The parchment shivered, and a new line appeared on its own.
describe:0.line: 'Can you *describe* the shape you see at the edge?'

rest:0.en: After three islands in one day, Bell dropped into the window seat and closed her eyes. 'We need *rest* before the crossing,' she murmured. The lantern above us swung gently. Outside, the star-sea glittered without care for tired navigators, but inside the cabin warmth it was easy to believe tomorrow could wait.
rest:0.cnHint: 小铃说，在渡过星海之前，我们需要好好____。
rest:0.hook: Then a soft knock came from the locked supply door.
rest:0.line: 'Even the best navigator needs *rest* before a long crossing.'

employer:0.en: Silverfang arrived uninvited, standing in the doorway of our cabin with a thin smile. 'Your *employer* sent me a message,' he said, glancing at Old Helm. Old Helm did not look surprised. He folded his hands slowly, the way he does when he is choosing every word with great care.
employer:0.cnHint: 银牙带来了关于老舵这个____的一条神秘消息。
employer:0.hook: Old Helm's next words came out quieter than I had ever heard him speak.
employer:0.line: 'Your *employer* asked me to deliver this in person.'

owner:0.en: In the corner of the cabin sat a small iron box that nobody had opened since I joined the troupe. Tonight Old Helm placed his hand on its lid. 'The *owner* of this box left it with me long ago,' he said quietly. The lock, I noticed, had already been undone.
owner:0.cnHint: 老舵告诉我，那个神秘铁盒真正的____曾经是他的老朋友。
owner:0.hook: Inside the box lay a single folded map and nothing else.
owner:0.line: 'The *owner* trusted me to open it only on this night.'

gender:0.en: Bell was studying the old crew records spread across the floor. 'Every entry notes age and island of birth,' she said, 'but not a single one records *gender*.' She tapped the page thoughtfully. It seemed the troupe had always cared far more about what a person could do than about anything else.
gender:0.cnHint: 小铃发现，老船队的记录从来不在乎成员的____。
gender:0.hook: One record at the bottom had been torn away entirely.
gender:0.line: 'Not one of these entries even mentions *gender* — interesting.'

website:0.en: Silverfang pulled out a thin glowing card and slid it across the table. 'My *website* has charts for every known island route,' he said pleasantly. Old Helm picked it up and studied it. The glow pulsed like a slow heartbeat. I had not expected sky-merchants to keep such careful records of places most people never believed existed.
website:0.cnHint: 银牙展示了他那个记录着所有岛屿航线的____。
website:0.hook: One route on the card led straight into the unmapped dark.
website:0.line: 'Everything you need is on my *website* — for the right price.'

emotional:0.en: Old Helm rarely showed feeling, so when his voice cracked while reading the old letter aloud, we all went still. 'Forgive me,' he said. 'I am being *emotional*.' Bell moved quietly to his side. The letter was from someone whose name none of us knew, yet the words filled the cabin like old music.
emotional:0.cnHint: 老舵在读那封信时，罕见地变得非常____。
emotional:0.hook: He folded the letter before any of us could read the signature.
emotional:0.line: 'I am sorry for being *emotional* — this letter is very old.'

training:0.en: I asked Bell how she learned to read star-charts so fast. She laughed softly and pointed to a worn logbook on the shelf. 'Three years of *training* under Old Helm,' she said. 'He made me name every star before breakfast.' The logbook's cover was so creased it looked like a map of its own.
training:0.cnHint: 小铃告诉我，她经历了三年的____才能如此熟练地读懂星图。
training:0.hook: She paused, then added that not every student had finished the course.
training:0.line: 'Three years of *training* — and I still find new stars each night.'

meanwhile:0.en: Old Helm spread the new map across the worn table inside the lantern room. Bell traced each glowing line with one finger. *Meanwhile*, Silverfang stood at the far window, watching the sky for the next island to rise from the dark clouds below.
meanwhile:0.cnHint: 老船长和小铃在灯室里研究地图，____，银牙在窗边凝望着星空。
meanwhile:0.hook: Then one of the glowing lines began to move on its own.
meanwhile:0.line: '*Meanwhile*, the stars are already moving — we cannot wait much longer.'

damage:0.en: A cold wind had pushed through a crack in the lantern room wall during the night. Old Helm knelt beside the cracked beam and shook his head slowly. The *damage* was worse than it looked — three map fragments had been soaked by rain and their ink was already running.
damage:0.cnHint: 夜里的寒风给灯室造成了____，珍贵的地图碎片被雨水浸湿了。
damage:0.hook: Bell held up the blurred fragment — and saw a shape no one had drawn.
damage:0.line: 'The *damage* to these maps may have cost us the only route forward.'

police:0.en: Old Helm pulled out a small brass badge from his coat and held it toward the doorman of the archive tower. 'Island *police* gave us clearance,' he said, steady and calm. The doorman studied the badge for a long moment, then stepped aside without a word.
police:0.cnHint: 老船长向档案塔的门卫出示了徽章，声称得到了岛上____的许可。
police:0.hook: Inside, every single shelf had been emptied the night before.
police:0.line: 'The island *police* granted us access — now please let us through.'

race:0.en: Bell called out from the upper deck, and everyone ran. The rival crew had spotted the same word-fragment drifting above the central plaza. It became a *race* — two teams sprinting along opposite bridges, boots loud on the iron planks, the glowing word drifting just out of reach.
race:0.cnHint: 两支队伍争相追抢漂浮的词语碎片，一场____就这样在空中桥上展开了。
race:0.hook: The word-fragment suddenly split in two equal halves.
race:0.line: 'This *race* will decide which crew earns the next island — run!'

medical:0.en: Inside the lower cabin, Old Helm opened a flat tin case and laid it on the bunk. It held small bottles and folded cloth — the troupe's *medical* kit, carried since the very first island. Bell had twisted an ankle on the iron bridge, and the crossing ahead could not wait.
medical:0.cnHint: 小铃在铁桥上扭伤了脚，老船长打开了船队的____箱为她处理伤口。
medical:0.hook: At the bottom of the tin lay a note none of them had written.
medical:0.line: 'Our *medical* supplies are low — we must restock before the next crossing.'

wear:0.en: Bell noticed it first — the soft *wear* on the edges of the old wooden door frame, where countless hands had touched it over many years. She pressed her palm to the groove and felt it hum faintly, as though the door remembered every traveller who had ever pushed it open.
wear:0.cnHint: 小铃注意到古老门框边缘的____痕迹，那里仿佛还留着无数旅人的记忆。
wear:0.hook: The humming grew louder the moment she spoke a word aloud.
wear:0.line: 'Feel this *wear* — this door has been opened by a thousand hands before ours.'

climate:0.en: The archive keeper was a small, quiet woman who had lived on the island for forty years. She told them the *climate* inside the tower was kept cold on purpose — warm air made the old word-maps curl and fade. Old Helm nodded and pulled his coat tighter around his shoulders.
climate:0.cnHint: 档案塔管理员解释说，塔内特殊的____是为了保护古老的词语地图。
climate:0.hook: She then whispered that one map had been warm to the touch all morning.
climate:0.line: 'The *climate* in here protects the oldest maps — please keep the door closed.'

head:0.en: Old Helm stood at the *head* of the long reading table, the lantern casting sharp shadows across his face. He placed the recovered word-fragment at the centre and looked at each member of the troupe in turn. No one spoke. Outside, the stars were already arranging themselves into a new path.
head:0.cnHint: 老船长站在长桌____，将找回的词语碎片放在中央，示意大家认真察看。
head:0.hook: The fragment pulsed once — and pointed directly at Bell.
head:0.line: 'As *head* of this troupe, I say we follow the map wherever it leads tonight.'

relate:0.en: Old Helm gathered us around the lantern table and began to *relate* the story of how the troupe first found a living word buried in river mud. His voice was slow and careful, each detail placed like a stone across water. By the end, the word 'current' glowed faintly on the map cloth, and a new island shimmered into view above the clouds.
relate:0.cnHint: 老舵在灯桌旁____着船团发现第一个词语的经历，地图上随之浮现出新的岛屿。
relate:0.hook: But one detail in his story did not match the map at all.
relate:0.line: 'Let me *relate* what happened the night we found the first word,' said Old Helm.

attitude:0.en: Bell stood at the prow of our little cabin-ship, chin lifted, arms loose at her sides. That *attitude* — open, calm, ready for whatever the sky might offer — was something I tried to copy every morning. Old Helm noticed and smiled. 'She has always faced new islands that way,' he said. 'It is how a navigator is born.'
attitude:0.cnHint: 小铃站在船头，以一种开放平静的____面对未知的岛屿，让叙述者深受感染。
attitude:0.hook: Then the ship tilted, and even Bell grabbed the rail.
attitude:0.line: 'Your *attitude* at the prow tells the sky you are not afraid,' Bell said softly.

fill:0.en: Silverfang had brought a crate of small glass bottles, and after supper we used them to collect starlight that pooled on the floor of the cabin. Each bottle could hold one colour of light. I watched mine *fill* slowly with soft blue, the glow rising like water. Old Helm said a full bottle could light any dark passage on any island we had not yet found.
fill:0.cnHint: 晚饭后，大家用玻璃瓶收集舱内积聚的星光，叙述者看着自己的瓶子慢慢被蓝光____满。
fill:0.hook: One bottle cracked, and the blue light poured straight through the floor.
fill:0.line: 'Watch yours *fill* before you seal it,' Silverfang warned, eyes on the glow.

ignore:0.en: A loud knocking came from the storage hatch below our feet. Old Helm told us to *ignore* it — just the wind pressing on loose boards, he said. But the knocking had a rhythm, almost like letters. Bell knelt and pressed her ear to the wood. When she looked up, her eyes were wide and bright. The map cloth on the table had already begun to shift.
ignore:0.cnHint: 储物舱传来有节奏的敲击声，老舵让大家____它，但小铃俯身细听后发现事情并不简单。
ignore:0.hook: The knocking spelled out a word none of us had collected yet.
ignore:0.line: '*Ignore* the noise for now,' Old Helm said, though his hand gripped the table edge.

necessary:0.en: Bell spread the map cloth flat and pointed to a blank space shaped like a sleeping bird. 'One more word is *necessary* before that island will appear,' she said. We had searched every shelf in the cabin and found nothing new. Then Silverfang turned over the old tea tin, and a folded slip of paper fell out. The word on it lit up the moment it touched the cloth.
necessary:0.cnHint: 小铃指着地图上的空白说，还____一个词语才能让那座岛出现，银牙意外地在茶罐底找到了它。
necessary:0.hook: The island appeared — but it was already moving away from us.
necessary:0.line: 'One more word is *necessary*; without it the island stays hidden,' Bell said.

definitely:0.en: Silverfang tapped the glowing word on the map cloth and grinned. 'This is *definitely* the one that opens the northern shelf,' he said. Old Helm crossed his arms and looked doubtful, but Bell was already spinning the cabin compass toward the new bearing. Outside the porthole, a ridge of pale light rose above the clouds, exactly where Silverfang had pointed.
definitely:0.cnHint: 银牙____地认为找到的词语能打开北方的新区域，尽管老舵将信将疑，但窗外的光芒证实了他的判断。
definitely:0.hook: The compass needle snapped clean off its post.
definitely:0.line: 'That is *definitely* the word we have been looking for,' said Silverfang, grinning wide.

forget:0.en: 'Whatever you do, do not *forget* the order of the words,' Old Helm said, pressing a small notebook into my hands. Each word had to be placed on the map cloth in the sequence we had found it, or the islands would rearrange themselves in the wrong pattern. I wrote every entry twice. The notebook felt heavier than it looked, as if the words inside were already dreaming of open sky.
forget:0.cnHint: 老舵叮嘱叙述者千万不要____词语的顺序，否则地图上的岛屿会错乱重排。
forget:0.hook: I checked the notebook and found one page completely blank.
forget:0.line: 'Do not *forget* the order — the islands depend on it,' Old Helm said quietly.

particularly:0.en: Old Helm went through each word on the map cloth, testing the glow with one finger. He was *particularly* careful with the pale green one near the centre, pressing it three times and watching the light bounce back. Bell said that green words were the hardest to hold — they faded if the cabin grew too warm. We turned down the lantern, and the whole cloth shone a little brighter.
particularly:0.cnHint: 老舵逐一检查地图上的词语，对中间那个浅绿色的词语____地小心，反复确认它的光芒。
particularly:0.hook: The green word dimmed anyway, and a whole island vanished with it.
particularly:0.line: 'Be *particularly* careful with the green ones — they are the first to fade,' said Old Helm.

land:0.en: Old Helm spread the old map across the table, tracing every ridge and valley with his finger. 'This floating island is small,' he said quietly, 'but the *land* beneath our feet holds three buried word-stones.' The lantern swayed, throwing gold shadows across the room.
land:0.cnHint: 老舵主在桌上展开地图，指出脚下的____藏着三块字石。
land:0.hook: Somewhere below the floorboards, something hummed.
land:0.line: 'The *land* here is full of old secrets, friends.'

promote:0.en: Bell pinned a fresh chart to the cabin wall, marking the troupe's new route in bright ink. 'A good path does more than move us forward,' she said, smoothing the edge. 'It can *promote* trust between the islands, letting strangers trade words instead of doubts.'
promote:0.cnHint: 领航员认为规划路线不仅能推进旅程，更能____各岛之间的信任。
promote:0.hook: One island on the chart had no name — only a question mark.
promote:0.line: 'A shared road will *promote* peace between us all.'

purchase:0.en: The night market inside the docking hall glowed with paper lanterns. Old Helm handed me a small coin carved from sky-coral. 'Your first *purchase* on the islands,' he said with a grin. I chose a tiny glass jar that held a single glowing word floating in blue light.
purchase:0.cnHint: 老舵主给了我一枚珊瑚币，让我完成在浮岛上的第一次____。
purchase:0.hook: The word inside the jar spelled something none of us recognised.
purchase:0.line: 'Every *purchase* here costs one coin and one memory.'

rely:0.en: The storm had bent our compass needle, and the stars outside the window were hidden by cloud. Bell stood very still, eyes closed. 'We cannot *rely* on instruments tonight,' she said softly, then opened her eyes and touched the warm word-stone on the table. 'We rely on this.'
rely:0.cnHint: 罗盘失灵，领航员说今晚我们无法____仪器，只能借助字石。
rely:0.hook: The stone pulsed once — and pointed east.
rely:0.line: 'We must *rely* on the stone when the stars hide.'

connect:0.en: Silverfang arrived at our cabin door carrying two halves of a broken map. Old Helm raised an eyebrow. Together they placed the pieces on the table, and the torn edges began to glow. 'Word-maps *connect* when the right hands hold them,' Silverfang said, almost gently.
connect:0.cnHint: 银牙带来破损地图，两人合力将其拼合，碎片____在了一起。
connect:0.hook: The joined map showed an island none of us had ever seen.
connect:0.line: 'Only trust can *connect* these broken pieces, old friend.'

indicate:0.en: Bell traced a thin silver line on the wall chart with her pen. The line curved toward a dim star cluster. 'These markings *indicate* a landing platform hidden inside that cloud band,' she said. Old Helm leaned close, squinting. Outside, the wind began to pick up speed.
indicate:0.cnHint: 领航员指出图上的标记____云层中藏着一处停靠台。
indicate:0.hook: The cloud band on the chart was moving — toward us.
indicate:0.line: 'The symbols *indicate* we have very little time left.'

period:0.en: Old Helm sat by the cabin window, polishing a word-stone that glowed deep amber. 'This stone comes from the *period* when the first troupe crossed the sky — before the islands had names,' he said quietly. I sat beside him, feeling the weight of all that old, patient time.
period:0.cnHint: 老舵主讲述字石来自浮岛还没有名字的那个____。
period:0.hook: The stone flickered, as though it remembered something painful.
period:0.line: 'That *period* shaped every island you see tonight.'

picture:0.en: I found a small wooden frame tucked behind the supply chest. Inside was a faded *picture* of a younger Old Helm standing on a bright island with people I had never met. He appeared at the doorway, looked at it for a long moment, then smiled — just a little.
picture:0.cnHint: 我在储物箱后找到一幅____，画中是年轻时的老舵主和陌生人。
picture:0.hook: In the corner of the picture, one face had been carefully covered.
picture:0.line: 'That *picture* shows where our long journey truly began.'

return:0.en: Inside the map room, Old Helm unrolled a worn chart across the table. 'Every word we find is a *return* — a path leading us back to where the sky first broke open,' he said softly. The lantern light caught the ink, and for a moment the whole room seemed to breathe.
return:0.cnHint: 老船长在地图室里说，每个词语都是一次____，引领我们回到天空最初裂开的地方。
return:0.hook: But one path on the chart led somewhere none of us had chosen.
return:0.line: 'Every *return* brings us closer to the sky's first wound,' said Old Helm.

remove:0.en: Bell knelt beside the navigation desk and carefully began to *remove* the old star-pins from the cloth map, one by one. Each pin left a tiny hole — a ghost of a journey already made. 'We carry the holes too,' she murmured, setting the last pin down with a quiet click.
remove:0.cnHint: 领航员小铃从布面地图上____旧的星形图钉，每个小孔都是曾走过的旅程留下的痕迹。
remove:0.hook: One hole, however, was not made by any pin she recognised.
remove:0.line: 'I must *remove* the old pins before the new path shows itself,' said Bell.

colleague:0.en: Old Helm poured two cups of warm tea and slid one toward me. 'You are a *colleague* now,' he said, 'not a guest.' The word landed heavier than I expected. Outside, the wind pushed gently against the hull, and the floating island rocked us like a slow, friendly hand.
colleague:0.cnHint: 老船长递给我一杯茶，说我现在是他的____，不再是过客了。
colleague:0.hook: Then he added something quiet that I was not sure I was meant to hear.
colleague:0.line: 'A *colleague* earns their place by listening first,' Old Helm told me.

normal:0.en: Nothing about our life felt *normal* — not the islands drifting above the clouds, not the words that glowed when you spoke them aloud. Yet sitting around the small stove that night, sharing bread and warm broth, everything felt exactly ordinary. I wondered if wonder, practised long enough, becomes its own kind of normal.
normal:0.cnHint: 漂浮的岛屿和发光的词语都不____，但围坐在火炉旁吃饭时，一切又感觉再平常不过了。
normal:0.hook: Until the stove light flickered — and shaped something on the wall.
normal:0.line: 'Nothing here is *normal*, and that is precisely why we stay,' said Old Helm.

succeed:0.en: Bell spread her notes across the floor and frowned. Three times she had tried to read the star-map; three times the pattern had slipped away. 'I will *succeed* this time,' she said, quiet and certain. She traced one line with her finger, and at last the whole map lit up like a held breath finally released.
succeed:0.cnHint: 小铃三次尝试解读星图都失败了，但她坚定地说这次一定能____，随后地图终于亮了起来。
succeed:0.hook: What it showed made her go very, very still.
succeed:0.line: 'We will *succeed* because we refuse to read the map alone,' said Bell.

image:0.en: Above the desk hung a small mirror, but it showed no ordinary reflection. Instead, a soft *image* of each island we had visited appeared, one after another, like memories sorting themselves. Old Helm said the mirror had come with the ship. Nobody knew who had made it, or what it was still looking for.
image:0.cnHint: 船舱书桌上方挂着一面镜子，里面出现了我们到访过的每座岛屿的____，仿佛记忆在自行整理。
image:0.hook: Tonight the mirror showed an island none of us had ever visited.
image:0.line: 'Every *image* in that mirror is a place still waiting for us,' said Old Helm.

ourselves:0.en: After the long day, we finally sat down and looked at *ourselves* in the small mirror — tired faces, ink-stained hands, hair full of wind. Bell laughed first. Then Old Helm. Then me. We did not look like heroes from any story. We looked exactly like people doing their best, and that was enough.
ourselves:0.cnHint: 漫长的一天结束后，我们在镜子里看了看____，都是疲惫的脸和沾满墨水的手，小铃笑了起来。
ourselves:0.hook: But the mirror added one extra reflection that did not belong to any of us.
ourselves:0.line: 'We have only *ourselves* and the stars — that has always been enough,' said Bell.

catch:0.en: I dropped the ink bottle and watched it roll toward the edge of the tilting desk. Everything slowed. Then Bell's hand shot out to *catch* it, one smooth move, not a drop spilled. She set it back without a word, gave me one small nod, and returned to her charts as if nothing remarkable had happened at all.
catch:0.cnHint: 墨水瓶从桌上滚落，小铃眼疾手快地____住了它，一滴都没洒，随后若无其事地继续看图表。
catch:0.hook: But her eyes, just for a second, had darted to the cabin door.
catch:0.line: '*Catch* every word before it fades — maps are made of moments,' said Bell.

mistake:0.en: Inside the map room, I spread our charts across the long table. Old Helm pointed to a mark near the edge. 'That symbol means danger, not shelter,' he said quietly. I had led us the wrong way for two days. Admitting the *mistake* felt heavy, but the room grew warmer once I did.
mistake:0.cnHint: 我向老舵主承认，自己在地图上犯了一个____，走错了两天的路。
mistake:0.hook: But the wrong path had led us somewhere the maps forgot.
mistake:0.line: 'A *mistake* is just the map showing you where to look next,' said Old Helm.

staff:0.en: The troupe gathered in the lantern room at the heart of our vessel. Old Helm introduced me to everyone — navigator, cook, keeper of words, and three others I hadn't met. 'This *staff* has crossed forty islands together,' he said proudly. Each face held a story I could not yet read.
staff:0.cnHint: 老舵主在船舱里向我介绍全体____，每个人都身怀一段故事。
staff:0.hook: One of them already knew my name before I gave it.
staff:0.line: 'Every member of our *staff* carries one secret word,' Bell whispered to me.

enhance:0.en: Bell sat at her desk, adjusting small crystal lenses over our star charts. She explained that each lens could *enhance* the faint lines drawn in stardust ink, making hidden routes appear. The room smelled of warm glass and old paper. I leaned closer and saw a path none of us had noticed before.
enhance:0.cnHint: 领航员用水晶镜片____星图，让一条隐藏的航路浮现出来。
enhance:0.hook: The hidden route pointed straight toward a sky no chart had named.
enhance:0.line: 'These lenses *enhance* the ink so the stars can speak,' said Bell.

famous:0.en: Old Helm unrolled a scroll above the fireplace and tapped a drawing of a tall silver tower. 'The Island of Echoes,' he said softly. 'It is *famous* for storing every word ever spoken under this sky.' I had heard that name in childhood songs. Now it sat on our route like a promise.
famous:0.cnHint: 老舵主告诉我，回声之岛以收藏天空下所有曾被说出的词语而____。
famous:0.hook: Only one word, they said, could open the tower door.
famous:0.line: 'It is *famous* not for its height but for what it remembers,' said Old Helm.

project:0.en: Bell had pinned dozens of small notes to the wall above her worktable. She called the whole effort the Starfall *project* — a plan to map every island that appeared only on nights when stars fell. I studied her notes until the lantern burned low. The idea was bigger than anything I had imagined joining.
project:0.cnHint: 领航员把她绘制星落之岛的____计划图钉满了整面墙。
project:0.hook: One island on her list had no coordinates — only a question mark.
project:0.line: 'The *project* started the night I saw three islands vanish at once,' said Bell.

record:0.en: Tucked behind the cook's shelf was a thin book with a cracked cover. Old Helm said it was the troupe's *record* — every island visited, every word collected, every sky condition noted. I turned the pages slowly. The earliest entries were written in a hand I did not recognise, careful and very small.
record:0.cnHint: 老舵主向我展示了记载全部旅程的____，最早的条目出自一个陌生的笔迹。
record:0.hook: The last entry stopped mid-sentence, the ink still fresh.
record:0.line: 'This *record* holds more courage than any story I could tell,' said Old Helm.

regular:0.en: Each evening the troupe held a *regular* meeting in the low-ceilinged room just off the main deck. Someone would read from the word collection, someone else would mark the day's travel, and Old Helm would end with a question no one was expected to answer. Tonight his question was: 'What are we not seeing?'
regular:0.cnHint: 每天傍晚，船队都会举行____例会，老舵主最后总会提出一个无人能答的问题。
regular:0.hook: Tonight, for the first time, someone actually had an answer.
regular:0.line: 'A *regular* meeting keeps the troupe from drifting apart,' said Old Helm.

security:0.en: The word vault was a small iron room bolted to the ship's core. Bell showed me the three separate locks and the soft hum of a crystal alarm woven into the walls. 'The *security* here matters,' she said, 'because a lost word cannot be spoken back into being.' I touched the door and felt the hum in my fingers.
security:0.cnHint: 领航员向我展示词库的____措施，因为一个失落的词语永远无法被重新说出。
security:0.hook: Yet someone had already been inside since morning.
security:0.line: 'Good *security* is not about locks — it is about care,' said Bell.

whatever:0.en: The map room was full of jars, each one holding a glowing word. Old Helm waved his hand over them and said we could take *whatever* we needed for the next crossing. I reached for a small jar near the back. Inside it, the word pulsed like a tiny star waiting to be used.
whatever:0.cnHint: 老舵告诉我们，地图室里的词语罐子，____我们需要的都可以拿。
whatever:0.hook: But one jar had no label, and it was already open.
whatever:0.line: 'Take *whatever* calls to you — the map knows what you need.'

predict:0.en: Bell spread the star charts across the wooden table and studied them with quiet eyes. 'I can *predict* where the next island will rise,' she said softly, tracing a silver line with one finger. Outside, the wind agreed, and the ship tilted gently toward a gap in the clouds.
predict:0.cnHint: 小铃看着星图，说她能____下一座岛屿将会出现的位置。
predict:0.hook: The line on her chart led straight into a storm no one had seen before.
predict:0.line: 'I can *predict* the next island, but not what lives on it.'

road:0.en: Inside the old waystation, a painted *road* covered the entire floor — a map of every island the troupe had ever crossed. Old Helm knelt down and touched a faded dot near the edge. 'That one nearly swallowed us whole,' he said with a quiet smile. I felt the weight of every step they had taken.
road:0.cnHint: 驿站地板上画着一条条____，记录着队伍走过的每一座岛屿。
road:0.hook: One painted road led off the floor and up the wall, still unfinished.
road:0.line: 'Every *road* on this floor was once just a word in a jar.'

solution:0.en: The lock on the inner door had six spinning rings, each carved with letters. Bell tried every pattern she knew. Then I noticed the word we had just collected glowing in my pocket. I held it to the rings — a perfect fit. Sometimes the *solution* is the thing you are already carrying.
solution:0.cnHint: 内门的锁难住了所有人，但我口袋里发光的词语竟然就是____。
solution:0.hook: The door swung open onto a room that should not exist.
solution:0.line: 'The *solution* was with us the whole time — funny how that works.'

total:0.en: Old Helm counted the jars on the shelf slowly, lips moving with each number. 'Forty-seven,' he said at last, then shook his head. 'We need fifty for the crossing. *Total* silence fell over the room. I looked at the empty spaces on the shelf and understood for the first time how much the journey still ahead of us would cost.
total:0.cnHint: 老舵数完架子上的词语罐后，____的寂静笼罩了整个房间。
total:0.hook: Three jars were missing, and the dust around them was fresh.
total:0.line: 'A *total* of forty-seven — three short of what we need.'

fail:0.en: The word-lantern above the table began to flicker. Bell adjusted the wick twice, but it kept dimming. 'If the light goes out, the map fades too,' Old Helm warned. We all leaned in, as if our closeness could help. I had never watched something *fail* so slowly, or cared so much about stopping it.
fail:0.cnHint: 地图室的词语灯开始变暗，小铃担心如果灯____熄灭，地图也会消失。
fail:0.hook: The last flicker of light spelled out a word none of us recognised.
fail:0.line: 'If the lantern *fails* tonight, we lose two weeks of the map.'

function:0.en: Silverfang arrived late, dropping a brass device onto the table without a word. It looked broken, but Old Helm turned it over gently and found a small switch. Suddenly it began to hum. 'Ah,' said Old Helm, 'now I see its *function*.' It was a compass — one that pointed not to north, but to the nearest unspoken word.
function:0.cnHint: 银牙带来了一个黄铜装置，老舵打开开关后终于明白了它的____。
function:0.hook: The compass spun once and pointed directly at me.
function:0.line: 'Its *function* is simple — it finds the words that are still lost.'

method:0.en: Bell had a *method* for sorting words: she hummed each one softly and listened for the sound it made against the jar. High notes meant the word was young. Low notes meant it had been waiting for a long time. I tried it myself, and one jar in the corner hummed so deep that the table shook. That word had been waiting for years.
method:0.cnHint: 小铃有一套整理词语罐的____，用哼鸣声来判断词语等待了多长时间。
method:0.hook: The deepest-humming jar had no slot on any map they owned.
method:0.line: 'My *method* is slow, but it has never chosen the wrong word.'

differ:0.en: Inside the map room, Old Helm spread three charts across the low table. Each one showed the same island chain, but the paths *differed* wildly — one curved south, one cut straight north, one spiralled inward like a shell. 'Only one is true,' he said quietly. We studied them in silence.
differ:0.cnHint: 老船长把三张地图摊在桌上，每条路线都____。
differ:0.hook: One wrong choice, and the islands vanish forever.
differ:0.line: 'These routes *differ* more than I expected — one of them is a trap.'

shape:0.en: Bell pressed her ear to the wooden wall and knocked twice, listening. Then she lit a candle and held it close. On the ceiling, a shadow appeared — the *shape* of a key, sharp and clear. 'There,' she whispered. 'That is where the next word is hidden.'
shape:0.cnHint: 贝尔用烛光在天花板上照出了一个____。
shape:0.hook: The shadow flickered, then slowly began to move.
shape:0.line: 'Look — that *shape* on the ceiling matches the old lock.'

twice:0.en: Old Helm read the parchment once, frowned, then read it *twice*. The second time, his finger stopped on a small mark near the corner — a star inside a circle. 'I missed that,' he muttered. Bell leaned over his shoulder. The whole room seemed to hold its breath.
twice:0.cnHint: 老船长把羊皮纸读了____，终于发现了角落里的记号。
twice:0.hook: That tiny mark could change everything.
twice:0.line: 'I have read this *twice*, and something is still not right.'

aspect:0.en: Silverfang stood in the doorway, arms folded. He had studied every *aspect* of the route — the winds, the tides, the star positions — and still he looked uneasy. 'The sky is wrong tonight,' he said at last. No one laughed. We all felt it too.
aspect:0.cnHint: 银牙船长仔细研究了路线的每一个____，却仍然感到不安。
aspect:0.hook: Something in the dark sky refused to be explained.
aspect:0.line: 'Every *aspect* of this route worries me — especially tonight.'

currently:0.en: I checked the glass dial on the shelf. It measured the pull of the island's core, and the needle was *currently* sitting far to the left — lower than any of us had seen before. Old Helm did not panic. He simply said, 'We have less time than I thought.'
currently:0.cnHint: 仪器的指针____指向一个令人担忧的位置。
currently:0.hook: Less time meant one decision had to be made right now.
currently:0.line: 'The dial is *currently* lower than it should ever be.'

decrease:0.en: Bell watched the candles. She had set twelve of them in a row at sunset. Now, two hours later, only seven still burned. The light would *decrease* all night, she warned, and once the last flame died the hidden writing on the wall would disappear with it.
decrease:0.cnHint: 贝尔警告大家，光线将会不断____，直到墙上的字消失。
decrease:0.hook: Six candles left, and the message was only half read.
decrease:0.line: 'If the light continues to *decrease*, we will lose the words.'

possibility:0.en: 'There is one more *possibility*,' said Old Helm, tapping the corner of the map where the ink had faded. 'A passage beneath the island — old, forgotten, maybe sealed.' Bell looked hopeful. Silverfang looked doubtful. I looked between them both and quietly began searching for a trapdoor.
possibility:0.cnHint: 老船长提出了最后一种____——岛屿下方可能有一条隐秘通道。
possibility:0.hook: My fingers found something cold beneath the rug.
possibility:0.line: 'There is still one *possibility* we have not tried yet.'

crucial:0.en: The star chart had one *crucial* detail the others lacked — a thin dotted line connecting two islands that appeared on no other map. Silverfang spotted it first. He said nothing, only placed his finger on the line and looked at Old Helm. The room went very still.
crucial:0.cnHint: 星图上有一个____的细节，其他地图上都没有。
crucial:0.hook: That dotted line led somewhere no one was meant to find.
crucial:0.line: 'This detail is *crucial* — without it, we are sailing blind.'

review:0.en: Inside the map-room, Old Helm spread every word-fragment we had collected across the wide table. 'Before we sail on, we do a *review*,' he said, tracing each glowing piece with one careful finger. By the time we finished, the fragments had arranged themselves into a new island shape none of us had seen before.
review:0.cnHint: 老舵主把所有碎片摊开在桌上，带领大家做出发前的____，碎片竟自动拼成了新的岛屿轮廓。
review:0.hook: The shape on the table matched no island on any chart we owned.
review:0.line: 'A good *review* before we leave keeps us from sailing blind,' Old Helm said.

ahead:0.en: Bell pressed her ear to the brass speaking-tube that ran through the hull of our little sky-ship. 'There is warm wind *ahead*,' she announced, eyes bright. Old Helm nodded and adjusted our course by half a turn. The stars beyond the bow window grew suddenly, beautifully closer.
ahead:0.cnHint: 小铃通过传声筒听到前方有顺风，老舵主调整航向后，前方星空变得格外璀璨。
ahead:0.hook: Something large and silent moved just beyond the warm wind's edge.
ahead:0.line: 'Clear skies *ahead* — we could reach the next island before dawn,' Bell said.

cheap:0.en: A vendor at the night market offered Old Helm a 'genuine star-chart' for almost nothing. Old Helm turned it over once and handed it back. 'A *cheap* chart costs more in the end,' he said quietly, 'when it sends you into the dark.' He paid three times as much for the honest one next door.
cheap:0.cnHint: 夜市小贩以极低的价格兜售星图，但老舵主婉拒了，认为____的东西最终代价更高。
cheap:0.hook: The vendor watched us go with an expression that was hard to read.
cheap:0.line: 'I never trust a *cheap* map — the mistakes are always expensive,' Old Helm said.

critical:0.en: The word-fragment we carried glowed red for the first time, right above a narrow bridge of cloud that connected two islands. Bell said the crossing was *critical*: if the cloud bridge dissolved before we were over it, we would have no path forward. We ran, and made it with seconds to spare.
critical:0.cnHint: 小铃警告云桥即将消散，这次穿越至____，大家拼命跑过去，险险赶在桥消失前到达。
critical:0.hook: Behind us, the cloud bridge folded silently into nothing.
critical:0.line: 'The timing is *critical* — we cross now or we turn back,' Bell said.

motivate:0.en: I was tired and ready to sit down when Silverfang pointed to a faint light blinking far below one of the upper islands. 'That light is a signal,' she said. 'Let it *motivate* you.' I did not fully understand, but I stood up anyway, and somehow my legs found their strength again.
motivate:0.cnHint: 银牙指着远处闪烁的神秘灯光，用它____了我，疲惫的我重新鼓起了力气。
motivate:0.hook: The light blinked twice more, then went perfectly still.
motivate:0.line: 'Let that light *motivate* you — someone out there is waiting,' Silverfang said.

charge:0.en: The night-lantern that lit our map-table had gone dark. Silverfang found a small crystal in her coat pocket and pressed it against the lantern's base. 'Island crystals *charge* anything that runs on star-light,' she explained. Within moments the lantern hummed back to life, flooding the room with gold.
charge:0.cnHint: 夜灯熄灭了，银牙用岛屿水晶给它____，灯立刻重新亮起，将整个房间染成金色。
charge:0.hook: The crystal cracked clean in two the moment the lantern reached full brightness.
charge:0.line: 'These crystals can *charge* a lantern in seconds if you know how,' Silverfang said.

complex:0.en: The new word we found that evening was unlike any other. Its shape kept shifting, folding in on itself like a puzzle that had no flat side. Old Helm studied it for a long while. 'This one is *complex*,' he admitted, 'but that only means the place it leads to will be worth finding.'
complex:0.cnHint: 新获得的词语碎片形状不断变化，老舵主研究了很久，承认它____，但也意味着目的地更值得期待。
complex:0.hook: When Old Helm finally placed it on the map, every other fragment began to tremble.
complex:0.line: 'The pattern is *complex*, but give me an hour and I will read it,' Old Helm said.

itself:0.en: We gathered around the speaking-tube as Bell played a single soft note on her small reed pipe. The tube carried the sound down into the island below us, and the island *itself* seemed to answer — a low hum rose through the floor, through our boots, all the way to our chests. We were heard.
itself:0.cnHint: 小铃吹响芦苇笛，悬浮岛屿____发出了回应，那低鸣穿过地板一路传到了我们的心口。
itself:0.hook: The hum shaped itself slowly into something that felt almost like a word.
itself:0.line: 'The island *itself* is speaking — listen carefully,' Bell said, eyes wide.

join:0.en: The map room felt too big for just three people. Old Helm spread the star-charts across the table and looked up at me with warm eyes. 'You are welcome to *join* us,' he said, sliding a blank piece of the chart toward me. I pressed my palm to the paper, and a faint glow told me I belonged here now.
join:0.cnHint: 老舵手邀请叙述者____他们的队伍，地图上出现了神奇的光芒。
join:0.hook: The glow on the paper slowly shaped itself into an arrow.
join:0.line: 'You are welcome to *join* us on every island we find.'

significant:0.en: Bell pinned a small glowing stone to the centre of the chart. 'This mark is *significant*,' she said quietly. Around it, three island names had appeared overnight, none of us knew how. Old Helm leaned in close, his breath fogging the cold glass of the lantern. The stone pulsed once, twice, then held steady.
significant:0.cnHint: 小铃指出地图上一个____的标记，它在一夜之间召唤出了三座岛屿的名字。
significant:0.hook: The third island name was written in a hand none of us recognised.
significant:0.line: 'This mark is *significant* — it showed up while we all slept.'

step:0.en: I heard Old Helm before I saw him. Each careful *step* across the wooden floor sent a soft creak through the map room. He was carrying a covered lantern and a folded letter. He set both down without a word. The letter, I noticed, had no name on it — only a pressed flower the colour of midnight.
step:0.cnHint: 老舵手迈着____走进地图室，带来了一封没有署名的神秘信件。
step:0.hook: He left the room before I could ask a single question.
step:0.line: 'Every *step* I take in here feels like it wakes the maps up.'

unique:0.en: Silverfang dropped a crystal shard onto the table. It rang like a small bell. 'Every island gives the troupe a token,' Old Helm explained, 'but this one is *unique* — no other island grows crystals that sing.' I turned it in my fingers. A tiny tune rose from it, soft and clear, filling the whole room with light.
unique:0.cnHint: 银牙带回一块____的水晶碎片，这种会唱歌的水晶只有一座岛屿才有。
unique:0.hook: The tune it played was the exact melody Bell had been humming all week.
unique:0.line: 'This crystal is *unique* — you will never find another one like it.'

inside:0.en: The storm had been fierce, so we stayed in. Bell spread her notes across the table and I finally saw what was *inside* the leather folder she always carried: dozens of hand-drawn island maps, each one tagged with a single word in red ink. Old Helm smiled at my wide eyes. 'Every word,' he said, 'is a door.'
inside:0.cnHint: 暴风雨中大家留在室内，叙述者终于看到了小铃皮革文件夹____的秘密地图。
inside:0.hook: One map had a word on it that matched the glow on my palm.
inside:0.line: 'Look *inside* the folder — every page there is a place we have been.'

majority:0.en: Old Helm counted the word-fragments laid out on the table. 'The *majority* of them point north,' he said, grouping seven shining pieces to one side and only two to the other. Bell circled the northern cluster on the chart with one quiet stroke of her pen. I felt the ship tilt, as if it had already decided.
majority:0.cnHint: 老舵手发现____的地图碎片都指向北方，小铃在海图上画下了一个圆。
majority:0.hook: The two southern pieces began to dim the moment the pen lifted.
majority:0.line: 'The *majority* of our words agree — we head north at first light.'

notice:0.en: I almost missed it. Pinned below the main chart was a tiny slip of paper. Old Helm did not *notice* it until I pointed; Bell had left a short message there three days ago. It read: 'When all words glow at once, look up, not down.' We looked at the ceiling. A star pattern had been carved there all along.
notice:0.cnHint: 叙述者____到地图下方藏着小铃三天前留下的纸条，上面的提示让大家抬头望向天花板。
notice:0.hook: The carved stars on the ceiling matched no sky any of us had ever seen.
notice:0.line: 'Did you *notice* the note she left? It changes everything we planned.'

taste:0.en: Bell handed me a small cup of the island tea she had brewed. One *taste* was enough: it was sweet, then sharp, then warm all the way down. 'Every island has its own blend,' Old Helm said, wrapping both hands around his cup. Outside the window, stars gathered close, as if they too wanted a sip.
taste:0.cnHint: 小铃泡了一杯岛屿特产茶，叙述者只____了一口便感受到了它独特的层次风味。
taste:0.hook: Old Helm set his cup down and pointed to a new star — one that had not been there before.
taste:0.line: 'One *taste* of this tea and you will remember the island forever.'

enormous:0.en: Inside the chart room, Old Helm unrolled the newest map fragment across the table. An *enormous* chandelier of captured starlight hung above us, filling every corner with silver glow. Bell traced the new island's outline with one finger, her eyes wide. The room felt too small for so much possibility.
enormous:0.cnHint: 团长在地图室里展开新地图碎片，头顶悬挂着一盏____的星光吊灯。
enormous:0.hook: But one edge of the map disappeared into a fold no one could open.
enormous:0.line: Old Helm: 'That *enormous* chandelier has guided this troupe for thirty years.'

pet:0.en: Bell kept a small sky-turtle she called Dot — her one *pet* aboard the airship. That evening, Dot crawled onto the navigation table and pressed a tiny claw onto a blank space on the chart. We all leaned in. The blank space slowly bloomed into the shape of a new island.
pet:0.cnHint: 领航员小铃养的____用爪子在海图空白处点出了一座新岛屿的轮廓。
pet:0.hook: Dot pulled her claw back and hid inside her shell without a sound.
pet:0.line: Bell: 'My *pet* has better instincts than any compass I own.'

restaurant:0.en: The troupe's common room doubled as a *restaurant* each evening, with folding tables and lanterns strung between the beams. Old Helm set down a bowl of starfruit soup in front of me and said nothing, which, Bell whispered, was his highest form of welcome. Outside, the islands drifted past like slow green thoughts.
restaurant:0.cnHint: 众人在兼作____的公共舱里用晚餐，团长亲手端来了星果汤。
restaurant:0.hook: Then the lanterns all swung in the same direction — toward something unseen.
restaurant:0.line: Old Helm: 'Every good *restaurant* needs a view worth remembering.'

driver:0.en: The airship's main wheel stood at the centre of the upper deck, and tonight it was my turn. Old Helm called me the *driver* of tomorrow, which made Bell laugh softly. I gripped the wheel, feeling the whole vessel breathe beneath my palms. The next island glittered at the edge of the dark.
driver:0.cnHint: 轮到叙述者掌舵，团长称他为明日的____，让领航员忍不住轻笑。
driver:0.hook: A second glitter appeared beside the first — something else was out there.
driver:0.line: Old Helm: 'A careful *driver* listens to the wind before steering.'

dream:0.en: I woke before dawn to find Bell sitting by the porthole, sketching. She said she had seen the next island in a *dream* — violet cliffs, a bridge made of cloud, and a word carved in letters each as tall as a person. She pressed the sketch into my hands. It was already warm.
dream:0.cnHint: 小铃告诉叙述者，她在____里看见了下一座岛屿的模样并画了下来。
dream:0.hook: The word carved on the cliff in her sketch was the same as my own name.
dream:0.line: Bell: 'Every island we find began as someone's *dream*.'

consumer:0.en: Old Helm spread the troupe's ledger on the table, tapping a line that tracked how much starlight fuel each member used. 'A wise *consumer* wastes nothing,' he said, circling my entry with a red pen. I had burned twice the usual amount chasing a false signal. The circle felt larger than it was.
consumer:0.cnHint: 团长翻开账本，指出叙述者是燃料的最大____，浪费了两倍用量。
consumer:0.hook: He closed the ledger and smiled — which was somehow worse than a frown.
consumer:0.line: Old Helm: 'A smart *consumer* of starlight never chases ghosts.'

interesting:0.en: Bell pinned a new phrase to the word-board above the navigation desk each morning. Today's card read simply: horizon. 'Not very *interesting*,' Silverfang said from the doorway, arms folded. Bell turned slowly. 'Then go find a better one,' she said. Silverfang picked up the card, studied it, and — without a word — pocketed it.
interesting:0.cnHint: 银牙起初觉得小铃今日选的词语不够____，却悄悄把卡片揣进了口袋。
interesting:0.hook: By noon, a new island shaped exactly like that word had appeared ahead.
interesting:0.line: Bell: 'The most *interesting* words are the ones that argue back.'

grade:0.en: The troupe sorted every collected word into three *grade* levels — common, rare, and radiant — kept in three separate wooden boxes under the chart table. Tonight Old Helm lifted the smallest box, the radiant one, and held it toward me. Inside, a single folded slip glowed faintly gold. My hand was already reaching.
grade:0.cnHint: 团长把收集的词语按____分成三档，今晚他打开了最高档的小木盒。
grade:0.hook: The gold glow pulsed once, then spelled out a location none of us knew.
grade:0.line: Old Helm: 'Every *grade* of word has its moment to shine.'

rule:0.en: Inside the map room, Old Helm spread a worn chart across the table. 'Every island follows a *rule*,' he said, tapping a faded circle at the edge of the page. 'Learn the rule, and the island opens like a door.' I leaned closer. The circle was blank — waiting for a word only we could find.
rule:0.cnHint: 老船长解释说，每座岛都有一条____，掌握它才能进入岛屿。
rule:0.hook: The blank circle began to glow the moment I touched it.
rule:0.line: 'Every island has a *rule*, and tonight we learn this one.'

plant:0.en: Bell kept a small shelf of green things above her navigation desk. Each *plant* had a tiny tag with an island's name on it. 'They grow when we get close,' she said, and I noticed one was already stretching toward the porthole, its leaves trembling with quiet excitement.
plant:0.cnHint: 小铃在领航桌上养着许多____，每株对应一座岛屿。
plant:0.hook: One plant turned sharply toward the dark window, though no light came from outside.
plant:0.line: 'This *plant* only blooms when its island is near — watch it closely.'

national:0.en: Old Helm unrolled a broad flag from a wooden case. It had no country's mark — just a ring of small islands stitched in silver thread. 'This is our *national* sign,' he said with a quiet pride, 'for the people of the sky roads.' I felt, for the first time, that I truly belonged here.
national:0.cnHint: 老船长展示了天路旅人的____旗帜，让叙述者感到归属。
national:0.hook: Another flag, almost identical, hung from a ship we had never seen before.
national:0.line: 'Our *national* symbol belongs to every soul who sails the sky roads.'

doctor:0.en: A stranger sat in the corner of the crew room, reading by lamplight. Old Helm introduced her as the island's resident *doctor* of star-charts — someone who studied the sky the way a healer studies the body. She looked up and said one word: 'Sit.' I sat, and she began to explain everything.
doctor:0.cnHint: 一位研究星图的____坐在角落里，即将向叙述者揭示重要信息。
doctor:0.hook: She closed the book and said the next island had never been mapped by anyone living.
doctor:0.line: 'I am a *doctor* of star-charts, and this one has a fever.'

economy:0.en: Bell showed me the ledger where she tracked each word the troupe collected. 'It is an *economy* of sorts,' she said, tapping the page. 'Words cost effort to find, and each one pays us with a new place to go.' I looked at the long list of names and felt the true weight of what we were building together.
economy:0.cnHint: 小铃把收集词语比作一种____，付出努力才能换来新的旅途。
economy:0.hook: One entry in the ledger was crossed out, and no one would say why.
economy:0.line: 'Words are our *economy* — spend them wisely and they open the sky.'

global:0.en: Old Helm's greatest map covered the whole inner wall of his cabin. It showed every floating island known to the troupe, linked by fine lines of silver ink. 'This is our *global* picture,' he said softly, 'and we are still drawing it.' I found one corner that was entirely empty and felt a pull I could not name.
global:0.cnHint: 老船长向叙述者展示了一幅____地图，但仍有一角空白待填。
global:0.hook: The empty corner seemed to shift slightly each time I looked away.
global:0.line: 'A *global* view reminds us how much sky is still ahead of us.'

leader:0.en: The debate over which route to take had lasted an hour when Bell finally set down her cup. Every eye moved to Old Helm. He was the natural *leader* of the troupe — not because he spoke loudest, but because he listened longest. He stood, pointed at a small unmarked island, and said: 'There.' No one argued.
leader:0.cnHint: 争论路线时，大家都看向作为____的老船长，等他做决定。
leader:0.hook: The island Old Helm chose had no name on any map the troupe carried.
leader:0.line: 'A good *leader* points the way, then steps aside to let the crew sail.'

scientific:0.en: Silverfang arrived at the map room door holding a glass jar of glowing dust. 'I took a *scientific* approach,' she announced, placing the jar on the table with great care. 'Samples, tests, observations.' Old Helm raised an eyebrow. Bell leaned forward. Inside the jar, the dust rearranged itself into the shape of an island none of us had ever seen.
scientific:0.cnHint: 银牙用____方法采集了发光尘埃样本，它们竟拼出了未知岛屿的形状。
scientific:0.hook: The dust island had a tiny door, and the door was open.
scientific:0.line: 'My *scientific* tests say this dust came from somewhere beyond our maps.'

decline:0.en: Inside the map room, Old Helm spread a worn chart across the table. 'Look here,' he said, tracing a line with one finger. 'Three islands have gone dark this season.' The chart showed a slow *decline* in safe routes — fewer stars marked, more gaps than before. I felt the weight of it. Somewhere out there, the sky was shrinking.
decline:0.cnHint: 老舵在地图室里向我展示安全航线正在____，可走的路越来越少。
decline:0.hook: One gap on the chart had no name at all.
decline:0.line: 'This *decline* in safe routes worries me more than any storm,' Old Helm said.

extra:0.en: Bell had pinned an *extra* map fragment to the wall beside the usual charts — one nobody had asked for, one she had found tucked inside a cracked lantern. 'It does not match any island we know,' she admitted, eyes bright with the mystery of it. Old Helm leaned in close and smiled for the first time all evening.
extra:0.cnHint: 小铃在地图室墙上多钉了一张____的地图碎片，那是她从一盏破灯笼里找到的。
extra:0.hook: The fragment showed a star that should not exist.
extra:0.line: 'I kept this *extra* fragment secret until I was sure it was real,' Bell said.

income:0.en: The map room doubled as a counting room on quiet nights. Old Helm recorded every trade — dried fruit, star-glass, carved bone tokens. 'Our *income* from last port was thin,' he said, pushing the ledger toward me. 'We need a new word soon.' I looked at the half-empty shelves and understood: words were not just maps. They were survival.
income:0.cnHint: 老舵在地图室里记账，告诉我上次停靠港口的____很少，我们需要尽快找到新词语。
income:0.hook: The ledger showed one entry crossed out in red.
income:0.line: 'Without a steady *income*, we cannot afford to keep the ship in the sky,' Old Helm said.

medicine:0.en: A small cabinet in the corner of the map room held more than charts. Bell opened it and showed me jars of pale powder and dried leaves. 'Island healers trade *medicine* for safe passage,' she explained. 'Old Helm always makes room for it.' One jar glowed faintly blue. I did not ask what it cured, but I quietly hoped I would never need it.
medicine:0.cnHint: 小铃打开地图室角落的小柜子，向我介绍船队用来以物换物的____，其中一罐还发着微光。
medicine:0.hook: The blue jar had no label, only a small warning mark.
medicine:0.line: 'Good *medicine* is worth more than gold on the outer islands,' Bell said.

private:0.en: Old Helm kept one drawer of the map room locked. Not with chains — just with trust. 'That is my *private* collection,' he told me when I glanced at it. 'Words I have not shared yet. Not because they are dangerous, but because the right moment has not come.' I nodded and looked away, suddenly aware that even maps have secrets.
private:0.cnHint: 老舵告诉我地图室里有一个抽屉放着他____的收藏，时机未到，他还不打算分享。
private:0.hook: Behind the locked drawer, something hummed very softly.
private:0.line: 'Every navigator needs a *private* map that belongs only to them,' Old Helm said.

side:0.en: The map room had a long window on one *side*, looking out over the dark between islands. Silverfang stood there, arms crossed, studying the stars. 'I count eleven lights that were not there last week,' he said without turning around. I pressed my face to the cold glass beside him. Eleven new lights. Eleven possible words waiting to be found.
side:0.cnHint: 银牙站在地图室一*侧*的长窗前，发现了十一盏上周还不存在的星光。
side:0.hook: One of the eleven lights blinked, then moved.
side:0.line: 'Stand on this *side* of the window — the view of the new stars is clearer,' Silverfang said.

air:0.en: Late in the evening the map room filled with a strange *air* — not cold, not warm, but charged, like the moment before rain on a summer island. Bell lit the navigation candles and they all bent toward the east at once. Nobody spoke. We all felt it: somewhere to the east, a new word had just woken up, and it was calling the ship home.
air:0.cnHint: 夜晚地图室里弥漫着一种奇特的____，蜡烛全部朝东倾斜，像是某个新词语在呼唤着大家。
air:0.hook: All five candles pointed east and would not be straightened.
air:0.line: 'There is something in the *air* tonight — a new word is close, I am sure of it,' Bell said.

consumption:0.en: Old Helm kept a careful log of star-glass fuel. 'High *consumption* this week,' he said, tapping the page. 'We burned through twice the usual amount just holding our position in the wind.' He looked up at me with calm eyes. 'Find a word before next dawn, or we drift.' I grabbed my coat and pushed through the map room door into the open sky.
consumption:0.cnHint: 老舵记录到这周燃料的____过高，告诉我必须在天亮前找到一个新词语，否则船会随风漂走。
consumption:0.hook: Outside the door, the wind was already pulling the ship sideways.
consumption:0.line: 'At this rate of *consumption*, we have fuel for one more day at most,' Old Helm said.

evidence:0.en: Inside the map room, dusty shelves held jars of glowing ink and old charts. Old Helm pointed to a faint mark near the ceiling. 'Look here,' he said quietly. 'This scratch is *evidence* that someone reached this island before us.' I felt a chill, then a thrill — we were not the first, but we might be the boldest.
evidence:0.cnHint: 老舵主在地图室天花板上发现了一道划痕，这是此前有人到过此地的____。
evidence:0.hook: But the scratch pointed toward a door no one had noticed.
