Silverfang shrugged, looking almost friendly for once. 'Years of practice and a great deal of patience,' he said, then turned back to his own deck.
method:1.cnHint: 老舵对银牙无声降落的____感到好奇，银牙给出了一个出人意料的答案。
method:1.hook: Silverfang paused, then added one quiet word: 'Tonight.'
method:1.line: 'What is your *method* for landing so silently on these islands?'

review:1.en: Old Helm spread the worn map across the market stones and called us close. 'Before we move on,' he said, 'we do a *review* of every word-fragment we have collected.' He pointed to each glowing piece in turn. I noticed a gap shaped like a crescent island I had never seen before.
review:1.cnHint: 老舵主让大家围坐在市场的石板上，对已收集的词语碎片做____，我发现地图上有一处空白。
review:1.hook: The crescent gap pulsed once, as if calling our names.
review:1.line: 'A careful *review* now saves us from flying blind later,' Old Helm said.

ahead:1.en: Bell climbed the tall signal post at the edge of the dock and shaded her eyes against the starlight. 'There is another island *ahead*,' she called down, voice bright with wonder. From below I could just make out a soft green glow floating in the dark sky, waiting for us like a lantern left on.
ahead:1.cnHint: 小铃爬上码头的高杆，望见了____方向漂浮着一座散发绿光的岛屿。
ahead:1.hook: The green glow blinked once, then began slowly drifting away.
ahead:1.line: 'Keep the bow pointed *ahead* and we will reach it before dawn,' Bell said.

cheap:1.en: A vendor at the night market tried to sell us a so-called word-fragment for three sky-coins. Old Helm turned it over in his fingers and shook his head. 'This is *cheap* glass, not a true fragment,' he said with a kind smile. The vendor looked away, and somewhere behind us Bell quietly laughed.
cheap:1.cnHint: 一个摊贩试图把假碎片卖给我们，老舵主认出那只是____的玻璃，并非真正的词语碎片。
cheap:1.hook: Yet the glass caught starlight and spelled out one real letter.
cheap:1.line: 'I have seen real fragments — this one is far too *cheap* to be true,' Old Helm said.

critical:1.en: The bridge between two drifting platforms began to crack under our feet. Bell shouted that the centre board was the *critical* piece — if it broke, the whole crossing would fall. Old Helm tossed her a rope without a word. She caught it, looped it around the board, and we crossed in ten quick steps.
critical:1.cnHint: 桥板开裂，小铃大喊中间那块木板是____的，老舵主扔出绳子，大家迅速通过。
critical:1.hook: Behind us the bridge gave way with a soft, echoing crack.
critical:1.line: 'That centre board is *critical* — hold the rope and do not stop moving,' Bell said.

motivate:1.en: I was tired and my pack felt heavy as stone. Silverfang appeared beside me, matching my slow steps. 'New member,' she said, 'let the next island *motivate* you. Every word we find there is a door no one else has opened.' I lifted my head, and somehow my pack felt lighter for the rest of the climb.
motivate:1.cnHint: 我疲惫不堪，银牙走到我旁边，用下一座岛屿的未知来____我继续前行。
motivate:1.hook: Above us, a door-shaped light flickered on the island's cliff face.
motivate:1.line: 'Let the mystery of the next island *motivate* you when your feet grow tired,' Silverfang said.

charge:1.en: At the sky-harbour a small ferry boat rocked at its post. The harbour keeper stepped forward and named his price. 'We *charge* two word-fragments per passenger,' he said, holding up two fingers. Old Helm counted our fragments, smiled, and handed them over without argument. We boarded as the stars shifted west.
charge:1.cnHint: 天空港口的渡船管理员说要____两枚词语碎片作为船费，老舵主数了数，欣然支付。
charge:1.hook: The ferry lifted off the dock before the last fragment hit the keeper's palm.
charge:1.line: 'We only *charge* two fragments — that is as fair as the sky itself,' the harbour keeper said.

complex:1.en: Bell unfolded a new section of the map and we all leaned in. The island ahead had a *complex* system of bridges, lifts, and hidden paths that looped back on themselves like a knot. Silverfang whistled low. Old Helm simply tapped the first path with one finger and said, 'We start here.'
complex:1.cnHint: 小铃展开地图新片段，前方岛屿的路线结构十分____，像一个难解的绳结。
complex:1.hook: One of the looping paths on the map seemed to move on its own.
complex:1.line: 'The layout looks *complex*, but every knot has one loose thread,' Old Helm said.

itself:1.en: We found the new word-fragment resting in a small hollow at the centre of the night market square. It gave off a soft hum, almost like it was breathing. 'The word chose the place *itself*,' Old Helm said softly. No one argued. I reached down and lifted it, and the whole sky seemed to lean in to watch.
itself:1.cnHint: 我们在夜市广场中央发现了新的词语碎片，老舵主说它是____找到了这个地方，整片星空仿佛都在注视着我们。
itself:1.hook: The moment I lifted it, a new island appeared on the horizon.
itself:1.line: 'The fragment found this hollow by *itself* — the sky has its own way of guiding us,' Old Helm said.

join:1.en: The night market on Driftstone Island glowed with paper lanterns. Old Helm spread our map across a barrel and traced a dotted line. 'Two paths *join* here,' he said, tapping the crossing point. I leaned in and saw it — where the roads met, a new island bloomed like ink on wet paper.
join:1.cnHint: 在漂石岛的夜市上，老船长发现地图上有两条路____在一起，指向一座新岛屿。
join:1.hook: The ink was still warm beneath my fingertip.
join:1.line: 'Two paths *join* here, and that crossing is our next destination.'

significant:1.en: Bell held the glowing word-fragment up to the starlight. The crowd around the night stall fell quiet. 'This one feels different,' she whispered. Old Helm nodded slowly. 'It is *significant*,' he said. 'More than a map piece — it is a key.' The fragment pulsed once, and a distant island lit the horizon.
significant:1.cnHint: 小铃感觉手中的词语碎片非同寻常，老船长认为它____，不只是地图碎片，更像是一把钥匙。
significant:1.hook: A second island answered with a faint, distant glow.
significant:1.line: 'This fragment is *significant* — it opens something far bigger than a door.'

step:1.en: The night-bridge between two islands was made of floating stones, each one glowing faintly. I watched Old Helm *step* from one stone to the next, unhurried, certain. 'The bridge only holds for those who trust it,' he called back. I took a breath, lifted my foot, and the first stone held firm under me.
step:1.cnHint: 老船长平稳地____上那座由漂浮石块组成的夜桥，告诉我只有信任它的人，桥才会承住他们。
step:1.hook: The third stone ahead flickered like a candle in wind.
step:1.line: '*Step* with confidence, and the bridge will meet you halfway.'

unique:1.en: Silverfang dropped a small jar on the market table. Inside swirled a colour I had never seen — somewhere between silver and dawn. 'Every island produces something *unique*,' she said proudly. 'This mist comes only from the Peak of Echoes.' Old Helm uncorked the jar and a faint melody drifted out into the cold night air.
unique:1.cnHint: 竞争船长展示了一种____的迷雾，它只产自回声峰，老船长一打开瓶盖，夜空中便飘出了轻柔的旋律。
unique:1.hook: The melody pointed, like a finger, toward the east.
unique:1.line: 'Every island is *unique*, but this mist is unlike anything else I have ever found.'

inside:1.en: The old lantern-keeper handed me a brass box at the edge of the night market. I shook it gently. Something rustled. 'Look *inside*,' said Bell, her eyes bright with curiosity. I lifted the lid and found a word-fragment nestled in blue cloth — our next map piece, waiting quietly as if it had always known I would come.
inside:1.cnHint: 老灯笼守护者给了我一个铜盒子，小铃让我看看____，结果发现了我们的下一块地图碎片。
inside:1.hook: The word on the fragment shimmered, then rearranged itself.
inside:1.line: 'Look *inside* — the answer is never as far away as you think it is.'

majority:1.en: At the crossroads stall, Old Helm asked our troupe which path to take. Bell pointed left; Silverfang pointed right. I looked at the crowd of travelers around us — the *majority* were heading left, lanterns bobbing in that direction. Old Helm smiled and chose right. 'The rare road,' he said, 'is always worth the extra steps.'
majority:1.cnHint: 在岔路口，大____的旅人都往左走，但老船长却选择了右边那条少有人走的路。
majority:1.hook: The right-hand path vanished into a cloud of silver fog.
majority:1.line: 'The *majority* may be right, but tonight I trust the road less traveled.'

notice:1.en: I almost missed it. The word-fragment was pressed into the bark of a lantern-post, no bigger than a thumbnail. It was Bell who grabbed my sleeve. 'Did you *notice* that mark?' she asked. I looked again and saw the faint glow. Without her sharp eyes, we would have walked right past our next destination into the dark.
notice:1.cnHint: 小铃让我____一个刻在灯柱上的发光标记——那是我们差点错过的下一块地图碎片。
notice:1.hook: Below the mark, an arrow pointed straight down into the cloud layer.
notice:1.line: 'Did you *notice* that mark on the post? We would have lost the trail without it.'

taste:1.en: The night-market baker pressed a small star-shaped cake into my hand — free, she said, for first-time visitors. I took a bite. The *taste* was warm and faintly sweet, like toasted grain and cool sky together. Old Helm laughed at my expression. 'Now you understand why travelers always return to Driftstone Island,' he said.
taste:1.cnHint: 夜市面包师送给我一块星形糕点，它的____让老船长笑着说，这就是为什么旅人总会重回漂石岛。
taste:1.hook: At the bottom of the wrapper lay a folded map fragment, still warm.
taste:1.line: 'The *taste* of this island stays with you long after the ship has sailed away.'

differ:1.en: The night market on Cloud Bridge *differed* from every island we had visited before. Here, traders sold bottled starlight and shoes made of pressed cloud. Old Helm spread his arms wide and grinned. 'Each island writes its own rules,' he said. Bell was already sketching the stalls into her map.
differ:1.cnHint: 云桥夜市与以往的岛屿____，老舵手兴奋地张开双臂。
differ:1.hook: But one stall had no goods — only a locked door and a humming sound.
differ:1.line: 'These customs *differ* from anything I have seen in thirty years of sailing,' said Old Helm.

shape:1.en: A lantern-maker on the open plaza was bending wire into every *shape* you could dream of — stars, fish, tiny ships. Old Helm bought one shaped like a compass rose. The moment he held it up, the lantern glowed gold and a new island appeared on Bell's chart, faint but real.
shape:1.cnHint: 广场上的灯笼师傅把铁丝弯成各种____，老舵手买了一个，新岛屿随即出现在海图上。
shape:1.hook: The lantern then flickered once and pointed north, all on its own.
shape:1.line: 'The *shape* of that island on the chart matches this lantern exactly,' Bell whispered.

twice:1.en: Bell rang the ship's bell *twice* — the signal that a new word had been found. I ran across the night-market square and nearly knocked over a cart of glowing fruit. Old Helm was kneeling beside a cracked cobblestone, brushing away dust to reveal letters pressed deep into the rock.
twice:1.cnHint: 贝尔敲了____下船铃，示意找到了新词语，我冲过夜市广场赶去查看。
twice:1.hook: The letters in the stone shifted, as though trying to rearrange themselves.
twice:1.line: 'I have rung this bell *twice*, so whatever is down there is important,' said Bell.

aspect:1.en: Every *aspect* of the night market felt alive — the smell of warm sugar, the hum of distant wind-harps, the way starlight pooled in the cracks between stones. Silverfang leaned against a railing and said it reminded him of the harbour town where he first learned to sail. For a moment his sharp eyes went soft.
aspect:1.cnHint: 夜市的每一个____都充满生机，就连竞争船长也陷入了温柔的回忆。
aspect:1.hook: Then Silverfang straightened up and said someone had been following us for an hour.
aspect:1.line: 'The most interesting *aspect* of this island is what it hides beneath the market,' said Silverfang.

currently:1.en: 'The bridge is *currently* closed after midnight,' the gate-keeper told us, holding up a lantern to study our faces. Old Helm smiled, pulled a small folded word from his coat pocket, and placed it gently on the gate post. The lock clicked open by itself. The gate-keeper stepped aside without another word.
currently:1.cnHint: 守门人说桥____不通行，但老舵手拿出一个词语碎片，锁竟然自己开了。
currently:1.hook: Beyond the gate, the bridge stretched into a darkness where the stars did not reach.
currently:1.line: 'The path we need is *currently* hidden, but a word will open it,' Old Helm said calmly.

decrease:1.en: As we climbed the stone steps away from the market, the noise began to *decrease*, replaced by a low wind carrying the scent of rain and pine. Bell counted the steps aloud — her habit on every new island. At step forty she stopped, pointed at a carved word in the wall, and whispered that we had found what we came for.
decrease:1.cnHint: 离开夜市后，喧嚣声逐渐____，贝尔数着台阶，在第四十级发现了刻在墙上的词语。
decrease:1.hook: The carved word pulsed once with pale blue light, then went still.
decrease:1.line: 'Watch how the star-count does not *decrease* as we climb — that means we are going the right way,' said Bell.

possibility:1.en: Old Helm unfolded the newest word and held it toward the sky. 'Every word is a *possibility*,' he said quietly. 'A door before it is opened.' Below us the night market glittered. Above us the stars were thick as spilled salt. I felt the word hum against my palm when he passed it to me, warm as a held breath.
possibility:1.cnHint: 老舵手展开新词语，说每一个词都是一种____，我接过词语时感到它在掌心颤动。
possibility:1.hook: Then the word folded itself into the shape of a key no one had asked it to make.
possibility:1.line: 'There is a *possibility* this word leads to an island no one in our troupe has ever seen,' Old Helm murmured.

crucial:1.en: Bell spread the chart on a night-market table and tapped one glowing point with her finger. 'This crossing is *crucial*,' she said. 'Miss it before dawn and the island drifts out of reach for a full season.' Silverfang was already heading for the ship. Old Helm scooped up the chart, and I ran after them both into the star-thick dark.
crucial:1.cnHint: 贝尔指着海图上的一个点说这次航行____，必须在黎明前出发，否则那座岛会漂走整整一季。
crucial:1.hook: The island on the chart was already moving — slowly, but moving.
crucial:1.line: 'Timing is *crucial* here — we leave now or we lose the island entirely,' said Bell.

enormous:1.en: The market square of Cinderrock Island stretched before us, lit by a hundred floating lanterns. At its centre stood an *enormous* stone clock, taller than three ships stacked together. Old Helm pressed his hand against it and smiled. 'The word is carved right here,' he said. We added it to our map, and a new island shimmered into view on the horizon.
enormous:1.cnHint: 在星落之夜的市集广场，团长发现了一座____的石钟，上面刻着新的词语碎片。
enormous:1.hook: But the clock's hands were turning backward, and no one knew why.
enormous:1.line: 'That *enormous* clock has not moved in a hundred years — until tonight.'

pet:1.en: A small stall near the edge of the square sold nothing but tiny glowing creatures in jars. Bell leaned close to one jar and laughed with delight. 'It looks just like a *pet* star,' she said. The creature blinked, and the word floated up from the jar like smoke, settling gently onto our map.
pet:1.cnHint: 小铃在街边摊位发现了一只像星星一样的____，它将一个新词语留在了地图上。
pet:1.hook: The creature's glow began to pulse faster, as if it was trying to warn us.
pet:1.line: 'Every navigator needs a *pet* like this — it always points toward the next island.'

restaurant:1.en: Old Helm led us down a narrow lane to a small *restaurant* built into the side of the island's cliff. The tables hung over open sky, and the stars looked close enough to touch. A folded menu on our table was not a menu at all — it was a map fragment with a new word printed in gold.
restaurant:1.cnHint: 团长带领大家来到悬崖边的____用餐，菜单竟然是一张新的地图碎片。
restaurant:1.hook: The waiter vanished before anyone could ask where the next island lay.
restaurant:1.line: 'Welcome — in this *restaurant*, every dish comes with a word and a new direction.'

driver:1.en: A cart rattled across the stone square pulled by two wind-filled sails on wheels. Its *driver* sat tall on a high bench, wearing a coat covered in small compass roses. She tossed Old Helm a rolled note as she passed. Inside was a single word and a rough drawing of an island we had never seen.
driver:1.cnHint: 一辆帆车的____向团长投来一张纸条，上面有一个新词和一座陌生岛屿的图样。
driver:1.hook: The cart was already gone, but its wheel tracks glowed faintly on the stone.
driver:1.line: 'I am the *driver* of the sky roads — follow the glow and you will find your next stop.'

dream:1.en: In the middle of the night market, an old woman sold bottled light. She said each bottle held a *dream* someone had left behind. Old Helm chose a small blue one, uncorked it, and a soft voice read out a word. The word landed on our map and the whole island seemed to breathe out slowly.
dream:1.cnHint: 夜市中，团长打开一瓶装着____的光瓶，里面传出的词语为地图添上了新的一角。
dream:1.hook: The blue light drifted upward and drew the shape of a door in the air.
dream:1.line: 'Every *dream* left in these bottles is a map waiting for the right traveller to open it.'

consumer:1.en: A trader at the far end of the square called out to anyone passing. 'Every *consumer* of starlight leaves a trace,' he said, pointing to the glowing footprints around us. He pressed a card into my hand. On it was a word, and below the word, an arrow pointing straight up toward a cloud island no one had noticed before.
consumer:1.cnHint: 一位商人告诉大家，每一个星光____都会留下踪迹，并递给我一张带有新词的卡片。
consumer:1.hook: Looking up, we saw the cloud island slowly beginning to drift away.
consumer:1.line: 'A wise *consumer* of starlight never wastes a single step on the wrong island.'

interesting:1.en: Bell found a noticeboard covered in papers, each one left by a traveller who had passed through before us. One paper was blank except for a single line: 'The most *interesting* island is the one you build with the words you collect.' Below it, folded small, was a map fragment we added to our growing chart.
interesting:1.cnHint: 小铃在公告栏上找到一张纸条，上面写着只有用词语碎片才能找到最____的岛屿。
interesting:1.hook: The handwriting on the note matched Old Helm's exactly.
interesting:1.line: 'Nothing is more *interesting* than a word that opens a door no one else can see.'

grade:1.en: Near the square's fountain, a judge sat at a small table scoring the lanterns that drifted past. He held up a card with a number each time. Old Helm asked what determined the *grade*. 'The brightness of the intention,' the judge said quietly, and handed us a slip of paper with tonight's highest-scoring word written on it.
grade:1.cnHint: 广场喷泉旁，一位评委向团长解释评分____的标准，并将今晚最高分的词语交给了我们。
grade:1.hook: The word on the slip was already glowing, and our map was pulling toward the east.

decline:1.en: Old Helm spread the star chart across the cold stone and pointed to the island's edge. 'Look,' he said quietly. The light towers along the western rim showed a steady *decline* — each lamp lower than the last, like steps leading somewhere dark below the clouds.
decline:1.cnHint: 老舵主指着星图边缘，发现西侧灯塔的光芒正在逐渐____。
decline:1.hook: Whatever waited below those clouds was rising toward us.
decline:1.line: 'This *decline* in the lights means the island is sinking,' Old Helm said.

extra:1.en: Bell handed out lanterns before we left camp. She counted heads twice, then reached into her pack and produced one *extra* lantern — small, dented, but burning steady. 'Islands like this one have a way of swallowing torches,' she said, hanging it on my belt without asking.
extra:1.cnHint: 小铃分发灯笼时，多拿出了一盏____的，挂在了我的腰带上。
extra:1.hook: She never explained why she had packed a spare.
extra:1.line: 'Take this *extra* lantern — trust me, you will need it,' Bell said.

income:1.en: At the crossroads market, Old Helm bartered three words from his satchel for a warm meal and a rough map. 'Our *income* is words,' he told me as we walked away, 'and we spend them only when the road demands it.' I held my own first word a little tighter.
income:1.cnHint: 老舵主告诉我，旅行团唯一的____就是收集来的"词语"。
income:1.hook: I wondered how many words it would cost to reach the next island.
income:1.line: 'Words are our *income* — spend them wisely on this road,' said Old Helm.

medicine:1.en: A child sat on the harbour steps, guarding a basket of small blue bottles. 'What are those?' I asked. 'Star-dew *medicine*,' she said proudly. 'Old Helm buys one every time the troupe passes through. He says the high winds give everyone sore throats.' She held one up to the lantern light.
medicine:1.cnHint: 港口台阶上，一个孩子守着篮子里的星露____，等待旅行团经过。
medicine:1.hook: The blue glow inside each bottle pulsed like a tiny heartbeat.
medicine:1.line: 'This star-dew *medicine* soothes every throat the wind has scratched,' she said.

private:1.en: Silverfang waited at the far end of the bridge, alone, back turned to the crowd. Bell leaned close. 'He keeps a *private* log of every island the troupe has ever visited — names, winds, secrets. He has never shown it to anyone.' Across the bridge, Silverfang tucked something small and leather-bound into his coat.
private:1.cnHint: 小铃悄悄说，竞争船长有一本从不示人的____航行日志。
private:1.hook: Tonight, for the first time, he was looking our way.
private:1.line: 'That is a *private* record — no one reads it but me,' said Silverfang.

side:1.en: We camped on the sheltered *side* of a great rock that jutted from the island's edge. The wind roared past the far face of it, but here the air was still and warm, thick with the smell of night-blooming moss. Old Helm said the troupe always rested on the quiet side before a crossing.
side:1.cnHint: 我们在巨岩背风的____扎营，远处的风声如同怒吼。
side:1.hook: Come morning, we would have to walk straight into that roar.
side:1.line: 'Always camp on the sheltered *side* — the crossing will be hard enough,' said Old Helm.

air:1.en: The moment we stepped onto the Night-fall Platform, the *air* changed. It tasted of cold metal and something sweet I could not name. Bell breathed in slowly, eyes shut, and smiled. 'That is the smell of a falling star passing close,' she said. 'It means the word we need is already near.'
air:1.cnHint: 踏上星落台时，小铃深吸一口____，说附近有一颗流星刚刚飞过。
air:1.hook: Somewhere just above us, something bright was dropping fast.
air:1.line: 'Breathe this *air* — a falling star has just passed over us,' Bell said.

consumption:1.en: Old Helm watched the island's great signal fire and frowned. 'The *consumption* of fuel is too fast,' he said. 'Three times the normal rate since last week.' Bell checked her compass. If the fire burned out, the sky-roads mapped from its light would vanish with it, and we would lose our path entirely.
consumption:1.cnHint: 老舵主担心信号火的燃料____过快，一旦熄灭，天空航路就会消失。
consumption:1.hook: The fire shuddered once, as if it had heard him.
consumption:1.line: 'This *consumption* of fuel will leave us blind in the dark,' Old Helm warned.

field:1.en: The troupe landed on a wide, flat island where the grass had been cut short and white lines painted across the ground. Old Helm called it a *field* — once a place where people raced and cheered, now silent under drifting stars. Somewhere beneath the grass, he said, a word was buried.
field:1.cnHint: 老舵主说，这片____下面埋着一个字。
field:1.hook: The ground trembled, and the painted lines began to glow.
field:1.line: 'Every *field* holds the memory of the crowd that once stood here,' said Old Helm.

personality:1.en: Bell studied the new map fragment with a careful eye. Each island, she explained, had its own *personality* — one island was bold and windy, another shy and wrapped in fog. Knowing an island's nature, she said, was the only safe way to land without trouble.
personality:1.cnHint: 领航员小铃解释，每座岛都有自己独特的____。
personality:1.hook: The next island on the map wore an expression no one could read.
personality:1.line: 'Its *personality* is wild and proud — we must land gently,' Bell warned.

size:1.en: From the deck, the island ahead looked small enough to hold in one hand. But as we sailed closer, its true *size* became clear — cliffs rose as tall as clouds, and forests spread as far as the eye could follow. Old Helm let out a low whistle.
size:1.cnHint: 靠近后，众人才意识到这座岛的____远超想象。
size:1.hook: Something enormous moved beneath the canopy of trees.
size:1.line: 'Never judge the *size* of an island from a distance,' Old Helm said quietly.

schedule:1.en: Bell pinned a new sheet to the mast each morning — the day's *schedule*, neat rows of tasks and times. Today it listed: repair the sail, trade for fruit at the next port, and reach the star-mirror island before dark. The troupe moved with purpose.
schedule:1.cnHint: 小铃每天早晨都会把新的____贴在桅杆上。
schedule:1.hook: Today's final task had no time written next to it — only a question mark.
schedule:1.line: 'The *schedule* says we dock before the second star rises,' Bell reminded us.

towards:1.en: A ribbon of light appeared on the horizon, pale gold and steady. Old Helm turned the wheel slowly, pointing the bow *towards* it without a word. The rest of us leaned forward, scarves lifting in the warm wind, as the light grew wider and the unknown came nearer.
towards:1.cnHint: 老舵主默默将船头朝____那道光驶去。
towards:1.hook: The light pulsed once, as if it had noticed us coming.
towards:1.line: 'We sail *towards* the light, whatever waits inside it,' Old Helm decided.

background:1.en: The new island rose steeply, and carved into the rock face behind the market stalls was a mosaic of coloured stone. Bell said the mosaic was the island's *background* — its history told in pictures so that even visitors with no shared language could understand where they had arrived.
background:1.cnHint: 小铃说，那面彩石马赛克记录着这座岛的____。
background:1.hook: One picture in the mosaic showed our own ship, though we had never been here before.
background:1.line: 'The *background* of this island is older than any map we carry,' Bell said softly.

department:1.en: The floating market was divided into bright sections, each with its own colour of lantern. The word-seller's *department* hung silver lanterns and kept the quietest corner of all. Old Helm led us straight there, past spice stalls and rope merchants, without stopping once.
department:1.cnHint: 字词商人的____挂着银色灯笼，是集市最安静的角落。
department:1.hook: The word-seller looked up before we arrived, as though she had expected us.
department:1.line: 'Welcome to my *department* — every word here wants to be found,' she smiled.

detail:1.en: Silverfang spread a rival map across a barrel and tapped one corner with a sharp finger. 'Your chart is missing a *detail*,' she said. A tiny symbol, shaped like a crescent, marked a passage between two storm clouds that our own map left blank. We had nearly flown into those clouds.
detail:1.cnHint: 竞争船长银牙指出，我们的地图上少了一个重要的____。
detail:1.hook: Silverfang rolled the map back up and did not offer to share it.
detail:1.line: 'One missing *detail* can send a whole ship off course,' Silverfang said flatly.

rule:1.en: The market square of Cinderstone Island glowed under a hundred lanterns. An old stone post stood at its centre, carved with the words: 'One *rule* governs this place — every trader must give a word before taking a word.' Old Helm pressed his hand to the post and smiled. 'Perfect,' he said. 'We already have plenty to trade.'
rule:1.cnHint: 石碑上刻着这里的____：每位商人必须先给出一个词才能换取一个词，老船长欣然接受。
rule:1.hook: But the last trader in the square had vanished, leaving only a single glowing coin.
rule:1.line: 'One *rule* governs this island, and tonight it works in our favour.'

plant:1.en: Bell led us off the main path to a narrow ledge where a single *plant* grew from a crack in the rock — its leaves silver, its tiny flowers shaped like open eyes. 'The islanders call it a sky-reader,' she said softly. Old Helm crouched beside it and whispered the word we had come for. The plant shivered, and a new map fragment drifted down like a leaf.
plant:1.cnHint: 贝尔带众人找到一株奇特的____，老船长轻声说出关键词后，它颤动着给出了一张地图碎片。
plant:1.hook: The silver leaves began to fold shut, as though the island itself was listening.
plant:1.line: 'Touch that *plant* gently — it remembers every hand that has ever reached for it.'

national:1.en: A wide banner hung across the gate of the Highbridge Island fair. It read: 'The *National* Gathering of Sky Traders — all islands welcome.' Old Helm spread his arms wide. 'Every troupe in the sky is here,' he said happily. Silverfang appeared beside us, arms crossed, already scanning the crowd for rivals. 'Then every word we need is here too,' I realised.
national:1.cnHint: 高桥岛集会的横幅上写着____空中商人大会，银牙船长也出现在人群中，让我意识到所有的词都近在眼前。
national:1.hook: Somewhere in that crowd, someone already held the word we needed most.
national:1.line: 'This *national* gathering only happens once every hundred star-turns — do not waste it.'

doctor:1.en: At the edge of the night market, a small tent glowed with warm yellow light. Inside sat a quiet woman surrounded by jars of pressed sky-herbs. 'I am the island *doctor*,' she said, 'but I trade in words, not medicine.' She pushed a tiny scroll toward us. Old Helm read it and laughed with delight — it was exactly the word that would open the next passage north.
doctor:1.cnHint: 夜市角落的____不用药物而用词语作为交换，她给了老船长一张小卷轴，正是打开北方通道的关键词。
doctor:1.hook: She watched us leave with an expression that suggested she already knew where we were going.
doctor:1.line: 'A *doctor* heals the body, but the right word heals a broken map.'

economy:1.en: The stone plaza of Saltwind Island was famous for one thing: its word-exchange board, where phrases were bought and sold like goods at a market. Old Helm studied the board carefully. 'The whole *economy* of this island runs on language,' he murmured, clearly impressed. Silverfang leaned in from behind. 'Then we are very rich,' she said, and for once she did not sound like a rival.
economy:1.cnHint: 盐风岛的广场以词语交易闻名，老船长感慨这里整个____都建立在语言之上，就连银牙也难得地表示赞同。
economy:1.hook: A single rare word on that board was worth more than all the coins in our pack.
economy:1.line: 'The *economy* of words never crashes — the rarer the phrase, the more it grows.'

global:1.en: Bell unrolled the largest chart I had ever seen across the deck of a docked sky-ship. It showed every floating island at once — a *global* view of the whole starlit world above the clouds. 'No one has ever mapped all of them,' she said quietly. Old Helm placed our newest word-fragment in the centre of the chart. Two more islands flickered into view, glowing faintly at the edge.
global:1.cnHint: 贝尔展开一张能呈现整个世界____视图的巨幅海图，老船长放上最新碎片后，又有两座岛屿隐约浮现。
global:1.hook: The two new islands pulsed with a light that matched the star directly above our heads.
global:1.line: 'A *global* map is only finished when the last word is placed — and we are close.'

leader:1.en: The crowd at the Driftstone crossroads parted for a tall woman in a coat covered with pinned word-badges. 'She is the *leader* of the Wordkeepers' guild,' Bell whispered beside me. The woman stopped in front of Old Helm and held out a sealed case. 'I have watched your troupe for three islands now,' she said. 'You have earned this.' Inside the case rested a single golden word-tile.
leader:1.cnHint: 漂石十字路口，文字守护者公会的____拦住众人，亲手将一枚金色词牌交给了老船长。
leader:1.hook: The word on that golden tile made Old Helm's hands tremble for the first time.
leader:1.line: 'A true *leader* does not hoard words — they know exactly when to pass them on.'

scientific:1.en: In the observatory tower at the peak of Glassridge Island, star-charts covered every wall. A young researcher looked up from her lenses. 'We use a *scientific* method to find new islands,' she explained, pointing to a row of careful measurements. 'Each star pattern maps to a word.' Old Helm copied her notes slowly, then held the page to the window. In the starlight, a new route shimmered into view.
scientific:1.cnHint: 玻璃岭岛观测塔的研究员用____方法寻找新岛屿，老船长抄下她的笔记后，在星光下发现了一条全新的航线。
scientific:1.hook: The route led straight toward a cluster of islands no chart had ever shown before.
scientific:1.line: 'Every *scientific* chart we make brings the last unmapped island one step closer.'

evidence:1.en: The market square of Driftstone Island was full of noise and colour. Old Helm knelt beside a cracked stone tile and pointed to faint blue marks. 'These are *evidence* that a word was here recently,' he said. I looked closer and saw the shape of letters slowly fading into the rock, like breath on a cold morning.
evidence:1.cnHint: 老舵手在石板上发现了某个词曾经存在过的____，那些蓝色印记正在慢慢消退。
evidence:1.hook: The marks were still warm under my fingertips.
evidence:1.line: 'These are *evidence* that a word passed through here last night.'

prefer:1.en: Bell spread three glowing route-stones across the old wooden table outside the tea stall. Each one hummed a different colour. 'I *prefer* the amber path,' she said, tapping the warmest stone. 'It always leads somewhere worth seeing.' I watched the amber light curl upward like a tiny flame reaching for the stars.
prefer:1.cnHint: 小铃在茶摊外摆出三块发光的路石，说她____走那条琥珀色的路线。
prefer:1.hook: The amber light suddenly flickered and pointed east.
prefer:1.line: 'I *prefer* the amber route — it has never once disappointed me.'

interview:1.en: A crowd had gathered around a storyteller near the harbour gate. Old Helm nudged me forward. 'Go and *interview* her,' he whispered. 'Ask what word she sang last night — the stars shifted when she did.' I stepped up, heart beating fast, and the old woman turned her bright eyes on me with a smile.
interview:1.cnHint: 老舵手让我去____码头边的说书人，问她昨晚唱出了什么词。
interview:1.hook: She leaned close and whispered a word I had never heard before.
interview:1.line: 'Go and *interview* the woman by the gate before she leaves.'

middle:1.en: The night market of Crestfall Square was packed with lanterns and noise. Right in the *middle* of the square stood a stone pillar, and carved into its top was a single glowing word. Bell grabbed my sleeve. 'That pillar is the island's heart,' she said. 'Whatever word rests there sets the mood for the whole place.'
middle:1.cnHint: 在广场____的石柱顶端，刻着一个会发光的词，据说它影响着整座岛的氛围。
middle:1.hook: The word on the pillar began to spin, slow and silent.
middle:1.line: 'Stand right in the *middle* — that is where the word shines brightest.'

standard:1.en: Old Helm unrolled a long chart covered in tiny symbols next to the spice stalls. 'Every word we collect must meet a *standard*,' he told me firmly. 'If it does not open a door or light a path, it is just noise.' I nodded, staring at rows of collected words glowing like small campfires across the old paper.
standard:1.cnHint: 老舵手解释说，每个收集的词都必须达到一定的____，否则就只是无用的噪音。
standard:1.hook: One word on the chart had no glow at all.
standard:1.line: 'Every word must meet our *standard* before it joins the map.'

subject:1.en: Silverfang stopped at a painted signboard outside the island's learning hall and read it aloud. 'Today's *subject* is the language of winds.' She raised an eyebrow at me. 'That is exactly the kind of lesson we need right now.' Inside, we could already hear a teacher's voice rising and falling like a sail in a breeze.
subject:1.cnHint: 银牙在学习堂外的告示牌前停下，上面写着今天课程的____正是他们需要的内容。
subject:1.hook: The door swung open before we even knocked.
subject:1.line: 'The *subject* today is the one thing standing between us and the next island.'

accept:1.en: The gate keeper of the Amber Steps crossed his arms and shook his head. Then Old Helm held out our newest word-fragment, still warm and faintly glowing. There was a long pause. At last the keeper reached out and took it. 'I *accept* this,' he said quietly. The gate groaned open and a warm wind poured through from the other side.
accept:1.cnHint: 守门人起初拒绝放行，直到老舵手拿出词语碎片，他终于____了这份通行凭证。
accept:1.hook: Beyond the gate, something enormous and bright was rising.
accept:1.line: 'I will *accept* this fragment — the path ahead is now yours.'

act:1.en: A small crowd watched a performer on a wooden stage near the well. Silverfang pulled us to a halt. 'Look at how she moves,' she said in a low voice. 'Every *act* she performs draws a word out of the air — watch the space above her hands.' I stared, and sure enough, letters were rising like sparks each time the performer swept her arms wide.
act:1.cnHint: 表演者的每一个____都能从空气中引出一个词，银牙让大家仔细观察她双手上方的空间。
act:1.hook: The next letter she drew was the one Old Helm had been searching for all week.
act:1.line: 'Every *act* she performs pulls another word straight out of the sky.'

estimate:1.en: The market square of Driftstone Isle hummed with traders selling bottled starlight. Old Helm studied the jars carefully, then turned to me. 'My *estimate* is thirty jars will get us to the next island,' he said, counting coins into his palm. We bought exactly thirty. The map fragment glowed the moment the last coin landed.
estimate:1.cnHint: 老舵在集市上对所需数量做出____，团队据此购买补给。
estimate:1.hook: But the map pointed somewhere none of us had ever heard of.
estimate:1.line: 'My *estimate* is thirty jars will get us to the next island.'

explore:1.en: Bell spread the new map fragment across a flat cloud-stone and traced its edges with one finger. 'We should *explore* the eastern ridge before dark,' she said quietly, eyes bright with curiosity. The rest of us grabbed our packs without a word. Whatever waited on that ridge, we were already walking toward it.
explore:1.cnHint: 小铃建议大家趁天黑前去____东边山脊。
explore:1.hook: A sound like distant bells answered us from the ridge.
explore:1.line: 'We should *explore* the eastern ridge before dark.'

fix:1.en: Our sky-raft tilted badly as we drifted over the Amber Shallows. Silverfang climbed onto the hull without being asked and began to work. 'I can *fix* this in ten minutes,' she called down, wrench already turning. Nine minutes later the raft was level, and a new word floated up from the water below like a bright fish.
fix:1.cnHint: 银牙主动爬上船体，声称能____这个问题。
fix:1.hook: The word in the water was still moving, as if alive.
fix:1.line: 'I can *fix* this in ten minutes,' she called down.

general:1.en: At the edge of Windgrass Plaza, Old Helm gathered us around a stone bench. He did not give orders. Instead he shared the *general* idea of the path ahead — wide open, full of unknowns, and probably wonderful. That was enough for all of us. We stepped off the plaza together as the stars shifted into a new pattern overhead.
general:1.cnHint: 老舵向大家介绍了前路____的情况，没有细说。
general:1.hook: The new star pattern matched no map any of us had ever seen.
general:1.line: 'Let me share the *general* idea of what lies ahead.'

loss:1.en: We found the old camp at Saltpeak Crossing abandoned — cold fire pit, a torn flag, no sign of whoever had been here. Old Helm picked up a faded journal from the ground. 'Every great journey carries some *loss*,' he said softly, tucking it away safely. Then he looked up and smiled. 'And every loss hides a door.'
loss:1.cnHint: 老舵在废弃营地捡到日记，感慨旅途中总有____。
loss:1.hook: The door Old Helm meant was carved right into the cliff face.
loss:1.line: 'Every great journey carries some *loss*,' he said softly.

partner:1.en: Silverfang had sailed alone for years before joining us. On the breezy docks of Coralspine Isle she watched Bell fix the navigation lantern, then said without looking up, 'You know, a good *partner* makes the stars easier to read.' Bell laughed and handed her the second lantern. They hung them together, and the dock lit up like a small sunrise.
partner:1.cnHint: 银牙在码头感慨，一个好____能让航行更轻松。
partner:1.hook: The two lanterns together cast a map-shaped shadow on the dock.
partner:1.line: 'A good *partner* makes the stars easier to read.'

concept:1.en: Bell pulled out the newest word-fragment and held it to the starlight. It read: BRIDGE. 'The *concept* is simple,' she said, turning it over in her hands. 'Every word we collect is a bridge to somewhere new.' Old Helm nodded slowly. I wrote it down in my notebook, because it felt like the truest thing anyone had said all journey.
concept:1.cnHint: 小铃解释道，她们收集单词的____其实很简单。
concept:1.hook: My notebook page began to glow the moment I wrote the word down.
concept:1.line: 'The *concept* is simple — every word is a bridge.'

history:1.en: At the center of Greymoss Square stood a pillar covered in carvings. Old Helm ran a hand along the stone. 'This pillar is the *history* of every troupe that passed through,' he said, pointing to small symbols pressed into the rock. I found a blank space near the bottom and pressed my thumb in softly. It felt right to leave a mark.
history:1.cnHint: 老舵说广场石柱记载着所有曾经过这里的团队的____。
history:1.hook: When I lifted my thumb, a new word was already glowing there.
history:1.line: 'This pillar is the *history* of every troupe that passed through.'

difficulty:2.en: Bell spread the star-map across a flat stone. One corner was torn away, leaving a gap where the eastern islands should have been. She traced the edge with her finger, her face tight with *difficulty*. 'We cannot plot a safe course without that missing piece,' she said softly.
difficulty:2.cnHint: 小铃在研究星图时遇到了____，因为地图残缺不全。
difficulty:2.hook: Somewhere in the dark, the missing piece was waiting.
difficulty:2.line: 'The *difficulty* is real — one wrong turn and we fall off the edge.'

full:2.en: Old Helm lifted the glass lantern and held it high. Inside, tiny fireflies circled in a slow, steady dance, filling every corner with a warm golden glow. The lantern was *full* of living light, enough to read any map, enough to push back the deepest shadow on the island.
full:2.cnHint: 老舵主举起一盏____光的灯笼，足以照亮最黑暗的角落。
full:2.hook: But something large out there was drawn to the glow.
full:2.line: 'A lantern *full* of fireflies — the sky gave us this gift tonight.'

range:2.en: From the high deck, I could finally see the whole archipelago laid out below like scattered coins. The *range* of floating islands stretched from the pale morning edge of the sky all the way to the deep purple dark where stars still burned. I had never felt so small, or so free.
range:2.cnHint: 站在高处，我第一次看清了浮岛群的整个____。
range:2.hook: At the far end of that range, one island glowed differently.
range:2.line: 'The *range* of islands ahead is wider than any map we carry.'

region:2.en: Bell pointed to a blank space on the map where no island name was written. 'This *region* has never been charted,' she said, her voice low and careful. The air around us felt different too — cooler, quieter, as if the sky itself was holding its breath just above that empty patch of cloud.
region:2.cnHint: 小铃指出地图上有一片空白____，从未被记录过。
region:2.hook: A faint hum rose from the clouds directly below us.
region:2.line: 'Every traveller who entered that *region* came back speaking in riddles.'

material:2.en: Silverfang dropped a bundle onto the deck with a heavy thud. Inside were strips of shimmering cloth woven from cloud-thread — the finest *material* on the floating islands, used only to repair the wings of sky-ships. Old Helm ran a hand across it and smiled for the first time in days.
material:2.cnHint: 银牙带来了一种珍贵的____，专门用来修复天船的翼帆。
material:2.hook: The cloth shivered as if it were still alive.
material:2.line: 'This *material* is rare — treat it better than you treat your own coat.'

pressure:2.en: The wind picked up without warning. The ropes groaned and the deck tilted sharply to one side. Bell called out that the air *pressure* was dropping fast — a sign the storm layer below us was rising. Old Helm gripped the wheel and nodded once, slowly, the way he always did before things got serious.
pressure:2.cnHint: 小铃警告说气____骤降，意味着下方的风暴层正在上升。
pressure:2.hook: The first crack of thunder reached us a moment later.
pressure:2.line: 'Feel that *pressure* in your ears? Hold on to something solid.'

thus:2.en: The word we had collected at dawn glowed faintly in Bell's palm. She pressed it gently onto the blank corner of the map. The edges of that empty space filled in at once — hills, bridges, a hidden harbour all appeared in soft ink. *Thus* the night gave us a new place to sail toward.
thus:2.cnHint: 小铃将收集到的词语贴上地图，____一处新的岛屿轮廓显现了出来。
thus:2.hook: The harbour on the map had a light burning in its window.
thus:2.line: 'We found the word, and *thus* the road finds us — simple as starlight.'

tool:2.en: Old Helm opened the small wooden chest he kept under the steering post. Inside, wrapped in soft cloth, lay a single brass needle that always pointed toward the nearest uncharted island. 'This is my most trusted *tool*,' he said, holding it up so we could all see it catch the starlight.
tool:2.cnHint: 老舵主展示了他最信赖的一件____，它总是指向最近的未知岛屿。
tool:2.hook: Tonight the needle was spinning, and it would not stop.
tool:2.line: 'Every good sailor needs one *tool* they trust more than their own eyes.'

international:2.en: Deep in the Archive Cloud, I found a stone tablet etched with symbols from a dozen island nations. Old Helm ran his fingers along the marks. 'This is *international* work,' he said softly, 'traders from every corner of the sky left their signs here.' The tablet hummed as if still carrying their voices.
international:2.cnHint: 我们在档案云中发现了一块刻满各岛符文的石板，老舵长说这是____性的遗迹。
international:2.hook: But one symbol had no island to match it.
international:2.line: Old Helm: 'This is *international* work — traders from every corner of the sky.'

manage:2.en: The bridge to the Ember Isle had split in two, a gap of cold wind between us and the far side. Bell studied the ropes, tested the planks, and tied three knots in quick order. Somehow she did *manage* to lash the broken halves together, and the bridge held just long enough for us all to cross.
manage:2.cnHint: 艾姆伯岛的桥断了，领航员想尽办法____把它临时接好。
manage:2.hook: The last plank fell into the clouds the moment Old Helm's boot left it.
manage:2.line: Bell: 'I will *manage* this — just give me the rope and some time.'

outside:2.en: We landed on a small ice platform and found a sealed glass cabin at its centre. A soft glow came from the *outside*, tracing the cabin's rim like a held breath. Old Helm pressed his ear to the wall and listened. 'Something inside is still awake,' he whispered, and none of us moved.
outside:2.cnHint: 我们在冰台中央发现了一个玻璃小屋，老舵长注意到____有奇异的光晕。
outside:2.hook: A slow tap answered from deep within the glass.
outside:2.line: Old Helm: 'Look at the *outside* — that glow was not there a moment ago.'

fun:2.en: Silverfang challenged us to a word-race across the Pebble Shelf: first to collect ten glowing letters wins. Old Helm laughed and called it pure *fun*, but I noticed he ran faster than anyone. We tumbled back together, pockets full of light, and Silverfang was already arguing about a rematch.
fun:2.cnHint: 银牙船长在卵石架上发起了文字竞赛，老舵长说这纯粹是一种____。
fun:2.hook: Then the letters in our pockets began to rearrange themselves.
fun:2.line: Old Helm: 'I admit it — this is more *fun* than I expected.'

reality:2.en: I had imagined the Star-Root to be enormous, a pillar holding up the whole sky. The *reality* was a small, quiet crystal no bigger than my fist, half-buried in soft moss. Old Helm knelt beside it and smiled. 'The quietest things,' he said, 'are often the ones doing the most work.'
reality:2.cnHint: 我以为星根会是庞然大物，但____却令人意外地平静渺小。
reality:2.hook: Yet when I touched it, every star above shifted one degree.
reality:2.line: Bell: 'The *reality* is always smaller and stranger than the story.'

beyond:2.en: From the rim of Driftstone Arch we could see the mapped islands clearly — and then, just *beyond* the last marker flag, a mass of green light that no chart had ever named. Bell pulled out her compass. The needle spun once and stopped, pointing straight at the green. Old Helm was already adjusting the sails.
beyond:2.cnHint: 在漂石拱门边缘，我们望见了所有地图标记之____处有一片绿色光芒。
beyond:2.hook: The compass had never pointed anywhere uncharted before.
beyond:2.line: Bell: 'Look — *beyond* the last flag, something the charts never named.'

completely:2.en: The ink-lantern we used to read the night map went out, and suddenly we were *completely* surrounded by dark. For a moment nobody spoke. Then a hundred tiny bioluminescent beetles rose from the moss below and lit the platform in blue, and Bell quietly said that was even better than a lantern.
completely:2.cnHint: 墨灯突然熄灭，我们____陷入黑暗，直到萤甲虫用蓝光将我们包围。
completely:2.hook: In the blue light, the map showed an island none of us had seen before.
completely:2.line: Bell: 'We are *completely* in the dark — but look what just woke up.'

advise:2.en: Before we sailed into the Hollow Gale, Silverfang pulled me aside. 'I *advise* you to tie every loose thing down and keep one hand on the rail at all times,' she said, almost kindly. It was the first time she had offered me any real help, and somehow that felt like its own kind of discovery.
advise:2.cnHint: 进入空洞风暴前，银牙船长把我拉到一边，____我做好充分准备。
advise:2.hook: She turned away before I could thank her.
advise:2.line: Silverfang: 'I *advise* you — tie everything down before we enter the Gale.'

attack:1.en: A sudden wind *attacked* the market stalls on the edge of Driftwood Plaza, scattering lanterns and paper maps in every direction. Old Helm grabbed my sleeve and pulled me under a canvas roof. 'Hold tight,' he said, laughing. When the gust passed, a single glowing word hung in the air where the lanterns had been.
attack:1.cnHint: 市集边缘突然刮来一阵狂风，____了所有的摊位，老舵手拉着我躲进布篷下。
attack:1.hook: The glowing word pulsed once, then began to drift toward open sky.
attack:1.line: 'That *attack* of wind just handed us our next map fragment, kid.'

heavy:1.en: The word-chest Bell pulled from the stone fountain was *heavy* — far heavier than it looked. She planted her boots wide and lifted with both arms while Silverfang counted aloud. I wedged my shoulder under one corner, and together we raised it onto the plaza cobblestones. A soft chime rang out, and the lid opened on its own.
heavy:1.cnHint: 贝尔从石头喷泉里拉出一只____的字箱，三个人合力才把它抬上广场石板地。
heavy:1.hook: Inside the chest, a single feather floated above a map no one had drawn yet.
heavy:1.line: 'It is far too *heavy* for one person — good thing there are three of us.'

thought:1.en: I stood alone at the edge of the night market, turning the new word-fragment over in my hand. My *thought* drifted to the road ahead — more islands, more open sky, more words waiting in strange corners. Old Helm appeared beside me, holding two cups of warm tea, and said nothing. He did not need to.
thought:1.cnHint: 我独自站在夜市边缘，____飘向前方那些未知的岛屿和等待被发现的文字。
thought:1.hook: The tea was still warm, and somewhere above us, a new island was rising.
thought:1.line: 'A good *thought* can be its own kind of map — hold on to that one.'

attract:1.en: The glowing word pinned to the notice board seemed to *attract* every traveller in the square. They pressed close, murmuring, reaching out but never quite touching it. Bell stepped through the crowd without a word and plucked it free. The crowd parted around her as if they had always meant to let her through.
attract:1.cnHint: 布告栏上那个发光的词____了广场上所有的旅人，贝尔却径直穿过人群将它取走。
attract:1.hook: The moment it left the board, a hidden door in the cobblestones clicked open.
attract:1.line: 'Bright things always *attract* curious eyes — move fast before the crowd grows.'

define:1.en: Old Helm crouched by the chalk marks someone had left on the plaza wall and tried to *define* the symbols for me. 'Each one is a place,' he said slowly, tracing the lines with one finger. 'And each place is a word.' I copied the shapes into my notebook, feeling the map grow a little larger inside my head.
define:1.cnHint: 老舵手蹲在广场墙边，试着为我____壁上那些粉笔符号的含义，说每一个都是一个地方。
define:1.hook: The last symbol he traced lit up faintly and began to hum.
define:1.line: 'Let me *define* this mark for you — it means the island changes shape at dawn.'

executive:1.en: The night market had its own *executive* — a tall woman in a coat covered with small brass keys who decided which traders could set up stalls and which words could be sold openly. She noticed our troupe the moment we arrived and crossed the square toward us with calm, deliberate steps. Old Helm straightened up and smiled his most careful smile.
executive:1.cnHint: 夜市有自己的____，一位身披铜钥匙外套的高个子女人，她一眼就注意到了我们的队伍。
executive:1.hook: She stopped two steps away and held out a key shaped like a question mark.
executive:1.line: 'As market *executive*, I decide which words leave this island — state your business.'

expectation:1.en: Every traveller who came to Lantern Crossing carried some *expectation* — a rare word, a shortcut to the upper islands, a rumour proved true. I had arrived hoping for all three. What I found instead was Bell sitting on a crate, sketching the stars, completely unbothered. 'Sit,' she said. 'The island gives what it gives.'
expectation:1.cnHint: 每位旅人都带着____来到灯笼渡口，而我发现的却是贝尔坐在箱子上平静地画星星。
expectation:1.hook: Then she turned her sketch around, and my name was written in the stars she had drawn.
expectation:1.line: 'Let go of *expectation* — the best words always find you when you stop chasing.'

friendly:1.en: The market keeper was *friendly* in the easy way of someone who has met ten thousand travellers and remembers every one. He handed Silverfang a steaming cup without being asked, refilled Old Helm's without interrupting his sentence, and slid a small wrapped word-fragment across the counter to me with a wink. 'New to the troupe?' he asked. 'You have that look.'
friendly:1.cnHint: 市场管理员对我们非常____，没等开口就递来热饮，还悄悄把一个词语碎片推到我面前。
friendly:1.hook: The wrapped fragment was still warm, and it smelled faintly of the next island.
friendly:1.line: 'Stay *friendly* with the market keepers — they always know which words arrived last night.'

indeed:1.en: The market square of Driftstone Island glowed under a roof of stars. Stalls sold bottled winds and dried cloud-petals. Old Helm picked up a small glowing card from a pile of map fragments and smiled. 'This is *indeed* what we need,' he said. The word on the card shimmered, and a new island lit up on our chart.
indeed:1.cnHint: 老舵在集市上找到了一张地图碎片，____证实了它正是troupe所需之物。
indeed:1.hook: The new island on the chart was already moving closer.
indeed:1.line: 'This is *indeed* the word that opens the eastern gate.'

launch:1.en: We gathered at the edge of Windbreak Pier before dawn. Bell had spent the night folding the sail into a special shape. At first light, Old Helm gave a short nod. The *launch* of our little sky-boat was quiet but perfect — the vessel rose smoothly, catching a ribbon of starwind, and the pier fell away below us.
launch:1.cnHint: 拂晓时分，troupe在码头完成了飞船的____，平稳驶入星风之中。
launch:1.hook: Something large and silent rose behind us from the mist.
launch:1.line: 'The *launch* must happen before the starwind shifts,' Bell said firmly.

refer:1.en: Silverfang unrolled a battered chart on the market cobblestones. Several island traders leaned in, arguing over routes. 'When you are lost,' Silverfang said, tapping the map, 'you must *refer* to the stars above and the words you have already found.' Everyone went quiet. I wrote that down in my notebook right away.
refer:1.cnHint: 银牙在市场上告诉众人，迷路时应____星图和已收集的词语。
refer:1.hook: One trader's eyes went wide — her own map showed something different.
refer:1.line: 'Always *refer* to the oldest word first — it will not lie to you.'

trust:1.en: The rope bridge between Twin-Peak Island and Cloudspine Island swayed hard in the night wind. Bell stepped onto it without hesitating. 'Your *trust* in the bridge is the bridge,' Old Helm told me with a warm look. I took a breath, gripped the rope, and walked. By the time I reached the other side, a new word was glowing in my palm.
trust:1.cnHint: 在摇晃的绳桥上，老舵教导我____是跨越险途的真正力量。
trust:1.hook: The bridge behind us dissolved into starlight the moment I crossed.
trust:1.line: '*Trust* in the word you carry — it chose you for a reason.'

discussion:1.en: We sat in a circle on the warm stone plaza of Amber Isle, a newly found word hovering between us like a small lantern. Old Helm, Bell, and Silverfang each read it aloud in turn. After a short *discussion*, we agreed it pointed south-east. I said nothing yet — I was too busy watching the word change colour as each voice touched it.
discussion:1.cnHint: 在广场上，troupe成员们围绕新词展开了一番____，最终确定了前进方向。
discussion:1.hook: The word stopped changing colour and looked straight at me.
discussion:1.line: 'Let us have a *discussion* before the word decides our route for us.'

extremely:1.en: The night market of Lantern Shelf Island floated on a wide platform of pale rock. Hundreds of glass jars held trapped starlight, casting long soft shadows. Old Helm called this place *extremely* rare — most travellers never found it, because the island only appeared when two moons aligned. I held my breath and tried to remember every detail.
extremely:1.cnHint: Lantern Shelf岛的夜市____罕见，只有双月重合时才会现身。
extremely:1.hook: The second moon was already beginning to slide away.
extremely:1.line: 'This spot is *extremely* hard to reach — write down everything you see.'

organize:1.en: After collecting three new words before midday, we were surrounded by glowing fragments spread across the courtyard floor. Bell crouched down and began to sort them by brightness. 'I will *organize* these by the direction they pull,' she said. Within minutes the fragments formed a rough map, and a path none of us had noticed before came clearly into view.
organize:1.cnHint: 小铃将收集到的词语碎片____好之后，一条隐藏的路径清晰呈现。
organize:1.hook: The path led straight to the edge of the island — and beyond.
organize:1.line: 'Let me *organize* the words — together they say more than apart.'

pattern:1.en: I noticed it first on the cobblestones outside the old word-vault: every fragment we had placed to dry in the sun had left a faint mark. Old Helm knelt and traced the shapes with one finger. 'A *pattern*,' he said softly. The marks formed a spiral that matched the edge of a whole new island on our chart, one we had never named before.
pattern:1.cnHint: 碎片在石板上留下的印记形成了一种____，正好与地图上一座未知岛屿的轮廓吻合。
pattern:1.hook: The unnamed island began to glow before Old Helm finished tracing.
pattern:1.line: 'Study the *pattern* of the marks — the next island is already written there.'

transform:1.en: The star-market of Driftstone Plaza hummed with traders at every corner. Old Helm held up a glowing word-shard and let its light spill across the cobblestones. Before our eyes, the plain grey tiles began to *transform*, shifting colour like the surface of a soap bubble until a whole new map blazed beneath our feet.
transform:1.cnHint: 老舵主让星石广场的地砖发生____，地图就这样浮现出来。
transform:1.hook: The map pointed somewhere none of us had ever dared to name.
transform:1.line: 'Watch the stones *transform* — the next island is hidden right below us.'

additional:1.en: Bell spread our word-shards across the market steps and counted carefully. We had enough to unlock the Amber Tier, but reaching the Sky Cradle beyond it would need one more. 'We require one *additional* word,' she said, scanning every stall with those sharp navigator's eyes.
additional:1.cnHint: 小铃数了数碎片，发现还需要一块____的词语碎片才能到达天空摇篮。
additional:1.hook: A vendor at the far stall smiled, as if she had been waiting for us.
additional:1.line: 'One *additional* shard and we reach the Sky Cradle tonight.'

journal:1.en: Outside the cartographer's tent, I found a worn book half-buried in starfall dust. Old Helm nodded when I lifted it. 'That is the troupe's *journal*,' he said softly. Every page held a word we had collected and the island it unlocked — a whole sky of adventures written in careful, looping ink.
journal:1.cnHint: 老舵主告诉我，那本沾满星尘的书是队伍的____，记录着每一个收集到的词语。
journal:1.hook: The last entry stopped mid-sentence, as though the writer had simply vanished.
journal:1.line: 'Every word we find goes into this *journal* — that is how we remember the sky.'

sort:1.en: Driftstone Plaza held every *sort* of trader — sellers of bottled wind, maps drawn on moth-wings, lanterns that hummed old tunes. Silverfang moved through them with easy confidence, testing each stall for the one thing we needed: a word-shard with a northern pull to it.
sort:1.cnHint: 银牙队长穿行在各____的摊贩之间，寻找带有北向引力的词语碎片。
sort:1.hook: Then one lantern flickered and spelled out three letters none of us recognised.
sort:1.line: 'This plaza draws every *sort* of trader — our shard is here somewhere.'

understanding:1.en: The old vendor asked why we collected words at all. I tried to explain — about the islands, the maps, the sky — but my words came out tangled. Old Helm placed a gentle hand on my shoulder. '*Understanding* comes when you see the first island open like a door,' he told her, and she smiled as if she already knew.
understanding:1.cnHint: 面对小贩的疑问，老舵主用____来解释为何要收集词语，而非长篇大论。
understanding:1.hook: The vendor reached under her counter and produced a shard that pulsed with quiet light.
understanding:1.line: '*Understanding* comes not from words alone, but from the doors they open.'

citizen:1.en: A young *citizen* of Driftstone blocked our path, arms folded, badge of the Island Council bright on her coat. She wanted to know who gave us the right to collect words that belonged to the plaza's sky. Old Helm produced our troupe seal, and her frown softened into curiosity.
citizen:1.cnHint: 一位飘石市的____拦住了我们，质问我们收集词语的权利。
citizen:1.hook: She glanced at the seal, then at the sky, and said nothing for a long moment.
citizen:1.line: 'Every *citizen* here guards these words — you need the council's mark to take one.'

contrast:1.en: The night market blazed with lantern-light, and the floating islands above it sat in near-darkness. The *contrast* was striking — fire and shadow trading places every few seconds as clouds drifted past. Bell said that kind of gap between light and dark was exactly how she read the sky for hidden passages.
contrast:1.cnHint: 小铃指出夜市的灯火与头顶岛屿的黑暗形成鲜明____，这正是寻找隐秘通道的线索。
contrast:1.hook: She pointed upward, and there — just where light met dark — a doorway trembled.
contrast:1.line: 'See that *contrast* between fire and shadow? That edge is where the passage hides.'

establish:1.en: Old Helm gathered us beside the plaza fountain and spoke quietly but clearly. Before we chased the next word, we needed to *establish* a meeting point — somewhere easy to find if the island fog rolled in and split the troupe apart. He pressed his thumb to the fountain's rim and left a glowing mark.
establish:1.cnHint: 老舵主要求我们先____一个集合点，以防海岛迷雾把队伍冲散。
establish:1.hook: The glow on the stone pulsed once, then spread like a root toward the horizon.
establish:1.line: 'We *establish* our meeting point here — if the fog takes you, come back to this fountain.'

describe:2.en: The old stone tablet glowed faintly on the cave wall of Ember Isle. 'Can you *describe* what you see?' Old Helm asked, holding his lantern close. I traced the carved lines slowly — a spiral of islands, each one waiting to be named. The word hummed under my fingers, and a new path lit up.
describe:2.cnHint: 在余烬岛的洞穴里，叙述者被要求用语言____石碑上的图案，一条新路由此点亮。
describe:2.hook: The final island on the map had no name — only a question mark.
describe:2.line: '*Describe* every detail you see, and leave nothing out,' said Old Helm.

rest:2.en: After three islands in one day, we landed on a small cloud shelf and dropped our bags. 'We need *rest*,' Bell said softly, wrapping her navigator's coat around her shoulders. The stars above were thick and quiet. Even the map fragments seemed to breathe slower. Tomorrow, the next word would find us.
rest:2.cnHint: 忙碌了一整天后，铃铛提议大家在云台上好好____，星空静静陪伴着疲惫的旅队。
rest:2.hook: But just before sleep, one of the map fragments began to glow.
rest:2.line: 'A little *rest* now means we fly faster tomorrow,' Bell said with a smile.

employer:2.en: A sealed letter was pinned to the mast when we woke. It was addressed to Old Helm. 'My *employer* hired your troupe for a reason,' it read, 'and that reason is closer than you think.' Old Helm folded the letter without a word. I noticed his hands were steady, but his eyes were not.
employer:2.cnHint: 清晨，桅杆上出现一封信，信中提到写信人的____雇用了这支旅队有特别的原因。
employer:2.hook: Old Helm burned the letter, but I had already memorised every word.
employer:2.line: 'My *employer* wants that word before anyone else finds it,' the letter warned.

owner:2.en: The amber lantern at the crossroads of Drift Market had no shop around it — just a sign that read: 'Ask the *owner* for the word.' We looked at each other. Silverfang stepped forward first, as always. A small figure rose from behind the sign, smiled, and handed us a glowing fragment without a word.
owner:2.cnHint: 漂流市场的路口有一盏无主的灯笼，据说只有找到它的____才能得到那个词语碎片。
owner:2.hook: The figure vanished before Silverfang could ask a single question.
owner:2.line: 'I am the *owner* of this light, and I have been waiting for you,' the figure said.

gender:2.en: The Archive of Winds kept records of every traveller who had ever passed through. Bell found our entry already written in faded ink. Name, origin, *gender*, skill — all listed, all correct. 'How does it know us?' I whispered. Bell ran her finger along the line and laughed quietly. 'It knows everyone,' she said.
gender:2.cnHint: 风之档案馆里早已记录了旅队每个人的信息，包括姓名、____和技能，令叙述者惊叹不已。
gender:2.hook: Below our names was a fourth entry — one none of us recognised.
gender:2.line: 'Name, *gender*, skill — the archive records it all before you arrive,' Bell said.

website:2.en: Tucked inside a cracked telescope on the observation deck was a tiny folded card. It showed a hand-drawn star chart and, at the bottom, an address written in glowing ink — a *website* for a place called the Sky Index. 'Someone left this on purpose,' Silverfang said, eyes narrow. I was already copying the address down.
website:2.cnHint: 在观测台的望远镜里，叙述者发现一张卡片，上面印着一个神秘____的地址，似乎是有人故意留下的。
website:2.hook: The Sky Index had exactly one page, and it was loading.
website:2.line: 'This *website* updates every time a new word is found,' Silverfang read aloud.

emotional:2.en: Old Helm held the fragment from the Singing Cliffs for a long time before he spoke. 'Forgive me,' he said, voice low, 'I get a little *emotional* here. My old troupe found their first word on this island.' He passed the fragment to me gently. The warmth in it felt like memory. I held it like I was holding his past.
emotional:2.cnHint: 在歌唱悬崖找到词语碎片后，老舵手变得有些____，因为这里有他旧日旅队的回忆。
emotional:2.hook: He never said what happened to that old troupe.
emotional:2.line: 'Do not laugh — I always get a little *emotional* when a new word lights up,' Old Helm said.

training:2.en: Bell set up a small rope course between two anchor posts on the deck at dawn. 'Your *training* starts now,' she told me, not unkindly. 'A navigator who can not move fast loses the word to the wind.' I slipped twice. The third run, I made it. Bell nodded once, and that small nod felt like a whole medal.
training:2.cnHint: 铃铛在甲板上为叙述者安排了____课程，告诉他只有行动够快才能抢在风前拿到词语。
training:2.hook: By the end, Bell said I was ready for the hardest island yet.
training:2.line: 'Your *training* is not about speed — it is about reading the sky before it speaks,' Bell said.

consume:2.en: Inside the hollow of a drifting island, we found a lantern that *consumed* oil at an impossible rate — a jar gone in minutes. Old Helm knelt beside it, reading faint symbols on the glass. 'This is no ordinary light,' he said. 'It burns a map into the air when it runs dry.'
consume:2.cnHint: 我们在一座漂浮岛的树洞里发现了一盏奇怪的灯，它____燃料的速度快得惊人。
consume:2.hook: The last drop fell, and the darkness ahead took shape.
consume:2.line: 'This flame will *consume* the oil — and then show us the way.'

desire:2.en: Bell pressed her ear to a smooth stone pillar near the island's edge. A low hum rose from inside. 'It is answering you,' Old Helm whispered. She closed her eyes. Whatever she *desired* most, the pillar seemed to mirror it back — a faint glow tracing the outline of a distant shore.
desire:2.cnHint: 小铃把耳朵贴在石柱上，据说石柱能感应到人内心最深处的____。
desire:2.hook: The glow pointed east, toward an island no map had ever named.
desire:2.line: 'Tell it what you *desire*, and it will light the path forward.'

meal:2.en: We gathered around a low fire on the Windgrass Shelf, sharing a *meal* of roasted roots and dried berries Old Helm pulled from his travel pack. Between bites, he unrolled a fragment of star-chart and smoothed it flat with his thumb. A new word shimmered at its centre.
meal:2.cnHint: 在风草台地，我们围坐一起吃____，老舵趁机展开了一张新的星图碎片。
meal:2.hook: The word on the chart pulsed once, then rearranged itself into coordinates.
meal:2.line: 'Eat your *meal* first — a clear head reads a better map.'

vegetable:2.en: Tucked inside a crate near the trading dock of Cloud Pebble Island, beneath bundles of dried *vegetable*, Bell found a rolled note sealed with silver wax. Nobody had addressed it to anyone. The handwriting was careful, old-fashioned — and the last line read: 'Leave this where the stars fall fastest.'
vegetable:2.cnHint: 小铃在干____下面发现了一张封好的神秘便条，末尾有一句令人费解的话。
vegetable:2.hook: Silver wax never lay in a forgotten crate by accident.
vegetable:2.line: 'Check under the *vegetable* bundles — things worth hiding go at the bottom.'

miss:2.en: A folded letter rested against the base of the Signal Spire, weighted by a smooth blue stone. It began: 'Dear *miss*, if you find this, the troupe has already passed the third arch.' Bell looked up at the arch above us. We had not yet reached the first.
miss:2.cnHint: 小铃在信号塔底部发现了一封信，开头称呼收信人为____，内容却暗示我们已经落后了。
miss:2.hook: Somewhere ahead, someone had expected us — and we were already late.
miss:2.line: 'Dear *miss*, the star you seek rises only once before dawn.'

yourself:2.en: The old instrument on the map table had one rule scratched into its frame: touch it *yourself*, or it shows nothing. Silverfang had sent three crew members to try. All three returned with blank faces and empty hands. Old Helm stepped aside and gestured to me. My turn.
yourself:2.cnHint: 地图桌上的古老仪器刻着一条规则：必须____触碰，否则它什么都不会显示。
yourself:2.hook: My fingertip hovered a breath above the cold brass surface.
yourself:2.line: 'You must do it *yourself* — it only answers the one who truly seeks.'

century:2.en: Carved into the underside of the Drifting Archive's stone door was a single line: this gate has opened once per *century*, at the moment a new word enters the sky. Old Helm traced the letters with two fingers. We had arrived on the right island. The question was whether we had arrived in the right hour.
century:2.cnHint: 漂浮档案馆的石门底部刻着一行字，说明它每____才开启一次，条件极为苛刻。
century:2.hook: Somewhere above us, a new star had just begun to fall.
century:2.line: 'Once a *century* it opens — and tonight, the sky is already moving.'

responsibility:2.en: Bell spread the recovered star-chart across the navigator's table. Every island we had lost track of glowed faintly on the parchment. 'This map chose us,' she said quietly. Old Helm placed his hand over the centre glow and nodded. Carrying it forward was our *responsibility* now, heavy and bright at once.
responsibility:2.cnHint: 贝尔展开星图，老船长点头，众人意识到守护地图是他们的____。
responsibility:2.hook: But one island on the chart had no name at all.
responsibility:2.line: 'This is our *responsibility*, and I will not let it fall.'

soon:2.en: A sealed bottle tumbled from a crack in the floating rock above us. Old Helm caught it before it shattered. Inside was a single folded note: 'We found the singing peak. Come *soon* — the stars here only stay until dawn.' Bell read it twice, her lantern swinging in the night wind.
soon:2.cnHint: 一只漂流瓶从岩缝落下，纸条上写着请他们____赶来。
soon:2.hook: Dawn on a floating island lasts only minutes.
soon:2.line: 'Come *soon*, or the path above the clouds will close.'

center:2.en: We drifted into a wide valley between two islands and found it there: a pillar of pale light rising from the *center* of a stone circle. Carved letters circled the base. Bell knelt and traced them with one finger, whispering each sound as if afraid the light might go out.
center:2.cnHint: 山谷中央石圈的____升起光柱，贝尔跪下轻声拼读刻字。
center:2.hook: The letters rearranged themselves the moment she finished.
center:2.line: 'Stand back — the *center* of the circle is shifting beneath us.'

arrive:2.en: The wind carried a scent of pine and warm bread — signs of island life. Old Helm checked his pocket compass and smiled. 'We *arrive* before the night market closes,' he said, and the whole troupe straightened up. Through the clouds below, coloured lanterns blinked like a string of small answers.
arrive:2.cnHint: 老舵手说他们会____，云层下彩灯闪烁，众人精神一振。
arrive:2.hook: Yet the island was not on any map we carried.
arrive:2.line: 'We *arrive* tonight, while the lanterns still burn bright.'

boost:2.en: Bell had been quiet all evening, her notes filled with crossed-out calculations. Then Old Helm showed her a second wind-stone he had kept in his coat. The extra pull it gave the sail was a real *boost*, and her pencil moved fast again, drawing a fresh route across the blank part of the chart.
boost:2.cnHint: 老舵手拿出风石，船帆获得额外____，贝尔重新振笔画出新航线。
boost:2.hook: The blank part of the chart hid the deepest sky of all.
boost:2.line: 'One wind-stone is a real *boost* when the current dies.'

conflict:2.en: Silverfang's vessel appeared from behind a cloud bank, flying a bright yellow pennant. Old Helm read the signal and frowned. 'He wants the same landing rock we do.' The two ships circled each other slowly, flags talking in short sharp waves. The gentle *conflict* of intentions hung in the air like held breath.
conflict:2.cnHint: 银牙船长与老舵手争夺同一块停靠岩，两船旗语____，气氛凝重。
conflict:2.hook: Then Silverfang did something no one expected — he turned away.
conflict:2.line: 'Our courses *conflict*, old friend, but let us not waste the wind.'

demand:2.en: The stone gate would not open by touch or by key. A carved mouth above the arch began to move. It spoke in slow, clear tones, and Bell translated in a hushed voice: 'It will *demand* a word that describes what you carry — not gold, not maps, but something no thief can lift.'
demand:2.cnHint: 石门开口____报出一个谜题，贝尔轻声翻译，众人陷入沉思。
demand:2.hook: Old Helm closed his eyes and whispered a single word.
demand:2.line: 'It will *demand* an answer only an honest heart can give.'

emotion:2.en: Old Helm opened the small wooden box we had carried since the first island. Inside was a pressed flower and a folded letter, neither addressed nor signed. He read it without a word, then closed the box gently. Whatever *emotion* moved across his face was brief, but it left the whole troupe standing in careful silence.
emotion:2.cnHint: 老舵手打开木盒读完信，脸上一闪而过的____让全团陷入沉默。
emotion:2.hook: He tucked the letter away and pointed toward the next star.
emotion:2.line: 'There is an *emotion* in this letter that only the sky understands.'

land:2.en: Bell spread the old chart across a barrel and pressed her finger to a blank patch near the edge. 'There,' she said. Every *land* we have visited so far sits on this side of the map. That empty space, she told us, was not a mistake — it was an invitation.
land:2.cnHint: 小铃在海图上发现了一片空白的____，说那不是错误，而是邀请。
land:2.hook: The blank space slowly began to glow.
land:2.line: 'Every *land* we have crossed so far was just a warm-up.'

promote:2.en: Old Helm called the troupe together at the edge of the island and held up a small silver badge. He pinned it to my coat with a nod. 'We *promote* those who listen before they leap,' he said. The stars above seemed to brighten at exactly that moment.
promote:2.cnHint: 老舵将一枚徽章别在我外套上，说懂得倾听的人才会被____。
promote:2.hook: The badge hummed with a soft, secret warmth.
promote:2.line: 'We *promote* those who listen before they leap.'

purchase:2.en: At the sky-market on Amber Isle, Bell traded three bottled winds for a rolled-up scroll. It was an odd *purchase* — the seller warned her it could only be read under starlight. She tucked it under her arm and smiled as if she already knew what it said.
purchase:2.cnHint: 小铃在天空集市上做了一笔奇特的____，买来一张只能在星光下阅读的卷轴。
purchase:2.hook: The scroll twitched, as if something inside it was alive.
purchase:2.line: 'This *purchase* cost three winds — it had better be worth it.'

rely:2.en: The bridge of vines between the two islands had begun to fray. Old Helm tested it with one boot and shook his head. 'We *rely* on this path every season,' he said quietly, almost to himself. He knelt and began to weave the loose strands back together with careful hands.
rely:2.cnHint: 藤桥开始老化，老舵说我们每个季节都____这条路，他开始动手修缮。
rely:2.hook: Halfway across, the whole bridge gave a long, slow groan.
rely:2.line: 'We *rely* on this path — so we must also mend it.'

connect:2.en: Bell discovered two stone pillars on opposite ends of the island, each carved with half a sentence. When she placed her palm on one, the carvings lit up and a thin thread of light began to *connect* the two pillars across the open sky. The air smelled of pine and distant rain.
connect:2.cnHint: 小铃发现两根石柱各刻着半句话，她触碰其中一根后，光线开始____它们。
connect:2.hook: The completed sentence spelled a name none of us recognised.
connect:2.line: 'Touch both stones and let the light *connect* them.'

indicate:2.en: Old Helm unrolled a thin copper sheet printed with dozens of tiny arrows. Each arrow pointed toward the centre of the sheet where a single island shape was drawn. 'These arrows *indicate* where the next fragment is hidden,' he said. I counted twelve arrows. They all agreed.
indicate:2.cnHint: 老舵展开铜片，说上面的箭头____着下一块碎片藏在何处。
indicate:2.hook: One arrow, unlike the rest, pointed straight up.
indicate:2.line: 'All these arrows *indicate* the same island — we leave at dawn.'

period:2.en: Bell found a log book wedged behind a loose stone in the wall. Its pages described a *period* of great storms that had once scattered the floating islands far apart. During those years, she read aloud, the troupe had kept going by collecting one word at a time.
period:2.cnHint: 小铃找到一本航海日志，记录了一段____，那时风暴将各岛吹散，船队靠收集词语坚持前行。
period:2.hook: The last entry was dated the very night I joined the troupe.
period:2.line: 'That *period* of storms is what made the troupe who they are.'

picture:2.en: Tucked inside the cracked lantern at the camp's edge was a small *picture* — ink on bark — showing three figures standing on an island that none of us recognised. Bell held it up to the starlight. Old Helm went very still, then said softly, 'I drew that years ago.'
picture:2.cnHint: 营地旧灯笼里藏着一幅____，画着三个站在陌生岛屿上的人影，老舵认出了它。
picture:2.hook: The island in the drawing matched the one on our next map.
picture:2.line: 'I drew this *picture* the night we first set sail together.'

relate:2.en: Old Helm spread the star-map across the deck and began to *relate* the story of the lost island to Bell and me. Each detail connected to the next like links in a chain. The stars above blinked as if they, too, were listening.
relate:2.cnHint: 老船长向大家____着失落岛屿的故事，每个细节都紧密相连。
relate:2.hook: But the last detail made Bell go very quiet.
relate:2.line: 'Let me *relate* what the old chart says, before the stars shift.'

attitude:2.en: Bell stood at the bow with a straight back and lifted chin — her whole *attitude* said she had no fear of the dark sky ahead. Old Helm watched her and smiled. 'That one was born for floating islands,' he said softly.
attitude:2.cnHint: 贝尔的____让老舵长感叹她天生就是为浮岛而生的。
attitude:2.hook: Then the wind turned, and even Bell's shoulders dropped a little.
attitude:2.line: 'Your *attitude* at the bow tells me you have sailed before.'

fill:2.en: We pulled open the old chest and found it packed with glowing fragments — enough to *fill* every blank corner of our map for weeks. Bell gasped. Old Helm simply nodded, as if he had always known such a treasure was waiting here among the stars.
fill:2.cnHint: 我们打开宝箱，发现里面的碎片足以____地图上所有空白处。
fill:2.hook: One fragment, however, was shaped like a door.
fill:2.line: 'These fragments will *fill* the map all the way to the edge.'

ignore:2.en: A soft chime rang from inside the locked lantern hanging at the mast. I tried to *ignore* it and keep sorting the map pieces, but the sound grew warmer and more insistent, as though the lantern itself had something urgent to say to me alone.
ignore:2.cnHint: 桅杆上的灯笼发出铃声，叙述者想____它，却发现声音越来越急切。
ignore:2.hook: When I finally looked, a tiny face was pressed against the glass.
ignore:2.line: 'Do not *ignore* that lantern — it only chimes when danger is close.'

necessary:2.en: Bell checked the rigging, tested the wind, then marked two words on the chart in red. 'Only these two stops are *necessary*,' she said firmly. 'The rest are pretty, but they will not get us to the night-fall island before the stars move.'
necessary:2.cnHint: 贝尔告诉大家，只有两个停靠点是____的，其余的都可以跳过。
necessary:2.hook: Old Helm crossed out one of her red marks without a word.
necessary:2.line: 'One stop is *necessary* — skip it and we lose the wind entirely.'
